stem: Henry gets a help desk call from Arthur in accounting who reports that his keyboard is not working. This seems like a familiar problem, one that another tech mentioned a short time back. Where should Henry look to find information on the problem?
explanation: Henry should check the incident reports to see if there’s a history of problems with the computer at that workstation. Incident reports record what happened and how it was resolved, which helps with repeat problems.
whyWrong: Change documentation records planned changes, not past problems with a device.
Asset management documentation tracks equipment, not the history of problems.
Risk management documentation assesses possible risks, not past incidents.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 28: Operational Procedures, Chapter Review question 1

stem: Annie wants to mark several Mac laptops issued to salespeople so that she can set up a scanner at the office door to track each time the laptops enter and leave the building. What will help her accomplish this goal?
options: Add a barcode sticker to each laptop.
Add an RFID tag to each laptop.
Submit a change document to the change board.
It can’t be done, because the laptops run macOS.
explanation: Annie should add a radio frequency identification (RFID) tag to each laptop and install a scanner at the door to track when the laptops are taken out of the office and returned. RFID tags can be read from a distance without a line of sight.
whyWrong: A barcode must be scanned at close range, so it cannot track laptops passing a door.
A change document is for planned changes, not for tracking assets.
The operating system does not matter for an RFID tag stuck on the outside of a laptop.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 28: Operational Procedures, Chapter Review question 2

stem: What broad term describes the process of creating a road map for current and future techs to make changes or repairs over time for an organization?
explanation: The term network documentation describes the road map for current and future techs to make changes or repairs over time for the organization. It includes diagrams, configurations, and procedures that later technicians can rely on.
whyWrong: Change documentation covers one change, not the overall road map of the network.
Change management is the process for making changes safely, not the road map of the network.
Management documentation is not a standard term for the road map of the network.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 28: Operational Procedures, Chapter Review question 5
note: 220-1102 4.1; network documentation is not listed under 220-1202 4.1, mapped to 220-1202 4.1 (types of documents).

stem: What does an IT department use for a departing employee to ensure that all equipment has been returned, access has been removed, and, where possible, knowledge transfer has been facilitated?
explanation: When an employee parts ways with an organization, the IT department uses an end-user termination checklist to ensure that the employee has returned all equipment, that their access has been removed, and, where possible, knowledge transfer has been facilitated. The 220-1202 objectives call this document the user off-boarding checklist.
whyWrong: A new-user checklist is used to onboard employees, not to offboard them.
A network topology diagram shows the layout of the network.
An acceptable use policy sets the rules for employees while they work there.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 28: Operational Procedures, Chapter Review question 10

stem: You have been given technical documentation from the network administrator that details the switch ports that you need to use for an upcoming network upgrade. Which of the following documents did you receive?
explanation: A network topology diagram shows network devices, such as switches and their individual ports (among other things.) This documentation is designed to help describe where computers and other networking equipment should connect, on a port-to-port basis. Often, a network topology diagram deals with physical connections, but it can also detail logical connectivity—for example, the IP addresses used by a LAN and what device that group of computers connects to. This might also be referred to as a logical topology diagram.
whyWrong: A change control form documents a proposed change, not switch port connections.
A process diagram shows the steps of a procedure, not the network ports.
A fiber backbone diagram shows high-speed links between networks, not individual switch ports.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 23
note: Network topology diagrams are not listed in 220-1202 4.1; mapped to 4.1 (types of documents).

stem: When a customer contacts a technician to report an issue, what practice should the technician employ to ensure the service ticket is correctly associated with the user?
options: Verify the customer’s identity then issue a unique ticket
Assign a random ticket number to maintain customer privacy
Use the technician’s personal identification as the ticket reference
Create a generic ticket without associating it with any user
explanation: To ensure accurate association between the reported issue and the user, the technician should verify the customer’s identity and assign a unique ticket identifying number. This identifier makes it easier to track and manage the reported issue throughout the support process.
whyWrong: A random number without verifying the user can link the ticket to the wrong person.
The technician's own ID does not identify the user who reported the issue.
A generic ticket cannot be tracked for a specific user.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 8

stem: After dedicating several hours to troubleshooting a computer problem for the company’s Chief Executive Officer (CEO), the technician is now pressed for time to resolve the issue promptly. What should the technician do as the NEXT step?
options: Engage in further research to address the problem
Restart the diagnostic process from the beginning
Notify the CEO that the repair may take a few weeks
Escalate the support ticket to higher-level technicians
explanation: Given the time constraint and the importance of resolving the issue promptly for the CEO, the technician should escalate the support ticket to higher-level technicians. By escalating the ticket, the technician ensures that the problem receives immediate attention from individuals with more expertise or resources to expedite the resolution process.
whyWrong: More research uses up time that the CEO does not have.
Restarting the diagnosis repeats work and causes more delay.
Telling the CEO it will take weeks does not meet the urgent need.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 30
note: 220-1102 4.1 and 4.7; mapped to 220-1202 4.1 (ticketing systems: escalation levels).

stem: When creating a comprehensive inventory of a company’s IT hardware, which documentation management method should a technician employ?
explanation: To effectively manage documentation while creating a full inventory of the company’s IT hardware, a technician should utilize asset tags and IDs. Asset tags and IDs provide a unique identification system that helps track and categorize each piece of hardware accurately. By affixing asset tags and assigning IDs to the equipment, the technician can easily associate specific hardware with corresponding documentation, such as purchase details, maintenance records, and warranty information. This ensures efficient inventory management and facilitates future hardware tracking and troubleshooting.
whyWrong: A new user setup checklist is for onboarding users, not for hardware inventory.
User information belongs in tickets and accounts, not the hardware inventory.
The procurement life cycle covers buying hardware, not tracking each item.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 78

stem: What do inventory management systems and software use to keep track of assets? (Select the two BEST answers.)
explanation: Asset tags and barcodes are used in inventory management systems and software to identify and keep records of company assets. Regulatory policies of an organization attempt to achieve compliance with a government’s objectives through laws and regulations. While you might interview users as part of your work, that would be to get information to help with troubleshooting, not for inventory management.
whyWrong: Regulatory policies aim at compliance with government laws; they do not identify individual company assets.
User interviews gather details for troubleshooting; they are not a way to track inventory.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: You are working at a help desk and encounter an issue that has not been identified or worked on previously. You go through your troubleshooting methodology, research, and, finally, solve the problem. Which of the following should you do so that the issue can be addressed properly if it is encountered again?
options: Add your findings to the knowledge base.
Enter the resolution into the ticket and close it.
Escalate the issue to your immediate supervisor.
Email the rest of the technicians on the team, explaining the problem.
explanation: You should add your findings to the knowledge base. Be sure to enter detailed information about the solution so that other techs can efficiently address the issue if they come across it in the future. You should also enter the resolution into the ticketing system and close that particular ticket so that you have proof of how you solved the problem. However, the trouble ticket system might not be easily searchable. The knowledge base, on the other hand, is designed for anyone to easily search by issue or by solution.
whyWrong: Closing the ticket records the fix, but tickets are hard to search, so others may not find the solution.
The problem is already solved, so there is no reason to escalate it to a supervisor.
Emailing every technician floods inboxes and does not store the solution where it can be searched later.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: Why is it important for the IT support ticket to ask for the error message?
options: To ensure the user feels satisfied with the response time
To charge for additional consulting hours
To speed up the process of identifying and resolving the problem
To close the ticket faster without needing more information
explanation: Speeding up the process of identifying and resolving the problem is best. Closing the ticket faster without needing more information is also true to an extent but is not a guarantee; the more information you can get up front, the less time you will take resolving the problem and the less time to resolution. In a large organization, some technicians specialize in certain problems, so it can also mean getting the right technician right away.
whyWrong: User satisfaction with response time is not why the ticket asks for the exact error message.
The error message helps solve the problem; it is not collected in order to bill extra consulting hours.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation, Cram Quiz question 3
note: The book keys two answers although the stem does not say how many to choose; its own explanation calls the second answer only partly true. Book answer kept.

stem: Why is a configuration management database (CMDB) important for managing IT assets?
options: It helps track the physical location of each asset.
It stores information about assets and their relationships, helping with problem solving and changes.
It limits the number of assets in the organization.
It ensures assets are used only by authorized users.
explanation: Information about assets and their relationships is stored in a configuration management database (CMDB). This helps with problem solving any issues when any changes are proposed. Although it can help with tracking down physical location, that isn’t the main goal of the CMDB. It will not limit the number of assets or their authorized users.
whyWrong: A CMDB can help find where an asset is, but tracking physical location is not its main purpose.
A CMDB records assets and their relationships; it does not limit how many assets an organization has.
Restricting assets to authorized users is done by access controls, not by a configuration database.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Why are service-level agreements (SLAs) important in IT service management?
options: They define the maximum amount of time a service can be down without affecting the business.
They set clear expectations between the service provider and the customer about response times and service delivery.
They restrict the number of incidents that can be reported by users.
They ensure that all IT staff are available 24/7 for support.
explanation: A service-level agreement (SLA) is a formal contract between any service provider (internal or external) and a customer (organization or individual). It defines the expected level of services, outlining the specifics of how services will be delivered. It includes key performance indicators, response times, and other metrics. By setting clear expectations and measurable goals, it improves customer satisfaction.
whyWrong: Maximum tolerable downtime is a business continuity measure; an SLA covers the expected level of service.
An SLA does not limit how many incidents users can report to the service provider.
An SLA sets agreed response times; it does not require all IT staff to be available around the clock.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: What is the FIRST step to consider when entering a ticket manually?
options: Determine the urgency of the issue.
explanation: Collecting user information is correct because it is essential to know who is reporting the issue and how to contact them. Determining the urgency of the issue is important, but communication to the customer is of higher importance. Identifying recent changes would happen after you enter the ticket. Verifying the issue description is an important, but secondary, step.
whyWrong: Urgency matters, but first you must know who is reporting the issue and how to reach them.
Recent changes are identified after the ticket is entered, during troubleshooting.
Verifying the issue description is important but comes after collecting the user information.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 1

stem: You just had an outage of Internet connectivity. Which document should you complete so that stakeholders understand the reason for the outage?
explanation: Incident documentation should be completed so that key stakeholders can understand the reason for the outage. Change management documentation is used for proposed changes to the network. Knowledge base articles are used to document symptoms and solutions. An acceptable use policy (AUP) is used to protect an organization's resources from user abuse.
whyWrong: Change management documentation covers proposed changes, not the cause of an outage.
A knowledge base article records symptoms and solutions for later use, not an outage report for stakeholders.
An acceptable use policy protects resources from user abuse and does not explain an outage.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 4

stem: Why is it important to document the root cause in an incident document?
options: To prevent the recurrence of the incident
explanation: Documenting the root cause helps in preventing the incident from recurring. There are typically no legal requirements around the documentation of the root cause, unless there is something specifically in a contract. Billing is also not related to documenting root cause, unless there is something specifically in a contract. Training new employees is important but is not a primary reason for documenting the root cause. When the cause is known and recorded, steps can be taken so that it does not happen again.
whyWrong: There is usually no legal rule to record the root cause, unless a contract says so.
Billing does not depend on recording the root cause, unless a contract says so.
Training new employees is useful but is not the main reason to record the root cause.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 6

stem: What is the primary benefit of having a knowledge base in an IT environment?
options: Reduces the number of help desk staff needed
Provides a quick reference for resolving common issues
explanation: Providing a quick reference for resolving common issues helps both users and technicians solve problems more efficiently. Creating a knowledge base rarely ever reduces help desk staff. Knowledges bases do not ensure compliance. Although knowledge bases are great tools, they do not improve morale.
whyWrong: A knowledge base rarely reduces the number of help desk staff.
A knowledge base does not ensure that people follow company policies.
A knowledge base is a useful tool, but it does not improve morale.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 10

stem: Which of the following is not a benefit of implementing asset tags for inventory management?
options: Scheduling the depreciation of the equipment
explanation: Scheduling of the depreciation of the equipment is performed in accounting software. Tracking of the equipment is a benefit to an asset tag. Identifying assets is a direct benefit of asset tags. An asset tag provides a proof of ownership.
whyWrong: Asset tags are used to track equipment, so tracking is a benefit.
Asset tags identify assets directly, so identifying is a benefit.
An asset tag serves as proof of ownership, so this is a benefit.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 20

stem: A helpdesk team is responsible for documenting and reporting any incidents that occur during their support activities. Which of the following documents should they use to record detailed information about each incident?
explanation: Incident reports are the appropriate documents for recording detailed information about each incident that occurs during support activities. They provide a structured format to document the incident, including the nature of the issue, the steps taken to resolve it, and any relevant details. Incident reports are essential for tracking, analysis, and compliance purposes.
whyWrong: Knowledge base articles hold reusable solutions to known issues, not the details of each individual incident.
Splash screens show a message before sign-in; they do not record anything about incidents.
Service-level agreements set response and resolution targets; they are not records of individual incidents.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.1 question 2

stem: Which of the following is an example of documentation that should be included in a support system information management plan?
explanation: Network diagrams provide visual representations of the network infrastructure and help support technicians understand the layout and connectivity, making them an essential part of the documentation for support system information management. The other choices are important but not directly related to support system information management.
whyWrong: Software licenses belong in asset management records rather than the support documentation plan the question describes.
Customer contact information belongs in the ticketing system, not in the infrastructure documentation the question asks about.
User passwords must never be recorded in support documentation, because that would expose the accounts.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.1 question 4
note: 220-1102 4.1; network diagrams are not listed in 220-1202 4.1, mapped to 4.1 (types of documents)

stem: In the context of support system information management, which of the following is the purpose of a knowledge base?
explanation: A knowledge base is a centralized repository of information that contains troubleshooting guides, FAQs, and solutions to known issues. It serves as a valuable resource for support technicians when resolving customer problems. The other choices are unrelated to the purpose of a knowledge base.
whyWrong: Customer feedback is gathered in surveys or the ticketing system, not in a knowledge base of solutions.
Hardware inventory is tracked with asset management tools and inventory lists, not a knowledge base.
Technician appointments are scheduled in a calendar or ticketing system, not in a knowledge base.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.1 question 5

stem: When documenting a support request, which of the following details should be included?
options: Date and time of the request
explanation: When documenting a support request, it is crucial to include the date and time of the request. This information helps establish the order of requests and allows for proper tracking and prioritization. The other choices are irrelevant details that do not contribute to support system information management.
whyWrong: A customer's favorite color has nothing to do with the support issue and does not belong in a ticket.
A technician's lunch preferences are irrelevant to the request and should not be recorded in a ticket.
Local weather conditions do not describe the issue and are not part of a support request record.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.1 question 6

stem: Which of the following is the best practice for managing support system documentation?
options: Storing documents in multiple physical locations
explanation: Regularly updating and reviewing documentation is a best practice to ensure that the information remains accurate and relevant. Outdated documents lead technicians to follow steps that no longer work, so documentation needs scheduled reviews and updates.
whyWrong: Keeping copies in several physical places causes version control problems because the copies drift apart.
Sending sensitive information by email can expose it to people who should not see it.
Printing only when necessary saves paper but does nothing to keep the documentation accurate.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.1 question 7

stem: Which of the following is an example of a ticketing system used in support systems?
explanation: ServiceNow is an example of a ticketing system commonly used in support systems. It allows support technicians to create, track, and manage support tickets, ensuring efficient resolution of customer issues. The other choices are software applications unrelated to ticketing systems.
whyWrong: Microsoft Office Suite is a set of productivity applications, not a ticketing system.
Adobe Photoshop is an image editing application and does not track support tickets.
Google Chrome is a web browser; it may open a ticketing system but is not one.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.1 question 8

stem: What is the primary purpose of a service level agreement (SLA) in support system documentation?
options: To outline the technician’s work schedule
To establish pricing for support services
To define response and resolution times
To determine the customer’s preferred contact method
explanation: A service level agreement (SLA) in support system documentation defines the agreed-upon response and resolution times for support requests. It sets expectations for both the support provider and the customer. The other choices are not directly related to the purpose of an SLA.
whyWrong: Technician work schedules are set by staff rosters, not by a service-level agreement.
Pricing is set in a contract or quote; an SLA defines service levels such as response times.
A customer's preferred contact method is recorded in the ticket or customer record, not defined by an SLA.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.1 question 9

stem: Which of the following should be included in a support system knowledge base article?
explanation: A support system knowledge base article should include tested solutions to known issues. It should provide accurate and reliable information to assist support technicians in resolving customer problems. The other choices are irrelevant or inappropriate for inclusion in a knowledge base.
whyWrong: Sales promotional material is marketing content and does not help technicians resolve issues.
Personal opinions are not reliable, tested information and do not belong in a knowledge base article.
Financial reports are business records and are unrelated to resolving support issues.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.1 question 10

stem: Which of the following is an example of a customer relationship management (CRM) system used in support systems?
explanation: Salesforce is an example of a customer relationship management (CRM) system used in support systems. It helps manage customer information, interactions, and support requests, ensuring a streamlined customer support experience. The other choices are unrelated to CRM systems.
whyWrong: Dropbox is a cloud file storage and sharing service, not a customer relationship management system.
Microsoft Word is a word processor and does not manage customer interactions.
Spotify is a music streaming service and has no customer relationship management function.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.1 question 12
note: 220-1102 4.1; CRM systems are not named in 220-1202 4.1, mapped to 4.1 (ticketing systems)

stem: In support system documentation, what is the purpose of creating an inventory list?
options: To keep an inventory of spare parts and equipment
explanation: Creating an inventory list in support system documentation helps track spare parts and equipment available for repair and replacement. It ensures that support technicians have the necessary resources to address customer issues effectively. The other choices are unrelated to the purpose of an inventory list.
whyWrong: Technician attendance is tracked by human resources systems, not by an inventory list.
Customer satisfaction ratings come from surveys and ticket feedback, not from an inventory list.
Maintenance tasks are scheduled in a calendar or maintenance plan, not in an inventory list.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.1 question 13

stem: A help desk technician takes a call from a user whose laptop cannot reach the network. The technician cannot solve it and must pass the ticket to a level 2 technician. Which action is BEST before escalating the ticket?
options: Record the user's contact details, the device information, and a clear description of the issue in the ticket
Close the ticket and ask the user to open a new one with the level 2 team
Set the ticket severity to high so that it is picked up faster
Email the level 2 technician a short note and leave the ticket empty
explanation: An escalated ticket must let the next technician continue without starting over. Clear user, device, and issue details mean the user does not have to repeat everything, and the work can be tracked from start to finish.
whyWrong: Closing the ticket loses the history and makes the user start again, which is the opposite of good escalation.
Severity should reflect the real impact on the user, not be raised just to jump the queue.
An email outside the ticket leaves no record in the ticketing system for tracking or later reference.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

stem: A technician has spent a full day solving an unusual printing error that no one on the team had seen before. The fix is now confirmed with the user. What should the technician do to BEST help others who meet the same error later?
options: Write a knowledge base article that gives the symptoms and the solution
Add a note to the printer's asset tag
Update the service-level agreement with the print vendor
Add the error to the new-user setup checklist
explanation: A knowledge base article records the symptoms and the solution in a searchable form. Other technicians and users can then fix the same issue quickly instead of repeating the research.
whyWrong: An asset tag identifies a device for inventory; it is not a place to record troubleshooting solutions.
An SLA sets service targets with a provider; it does not document how to fix a specific error.
The new-user checklist covers setting up new employees, not the fixes for technical problems.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

stem: An IT manager is asked which servers and applications would be affected if a database server is taken offline for an upgrade. The company tracks its hardware only with purchase records from accounting. Which of the following would BEST answer this kind of question in the future?
options: An inventory spreadsheet of spare parts
Barcode asset tags on each server
explanation: A CMDB stores configuration items and the relationships between them. It shows which systems depend on one another, so the impact of a change or an outage can be seen quickly.
whyWrong: An inventory list counts items such as spare parts; it does not show how systems depend on each other.
Asset tags identify individual devices but do not record which applications rely on which servers.
An off-boarding checklist removes a departing user's access and has nothing to do with system dependencies.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

stem: Joan has proposed upgrading the inkjet printers in the marketing department with color laser printers. The purpose of the change is to reduce the cost per page printed, because toner is less expensive than ink and the duty cycle of laser printers is longer than that of inkjet printers. The marketing department currently has three inkjet printers. What’s her logical NEXT step?
options: She should complete the scope of change part of the change document to factor in the price of the printers.
She should perform a risk analysis to determine any potentially negative consequences.
She should download the documentation on the new printers and begin the education process for the marketing department on how to use them.
She should contact the change board with her initial proposal.
explanation: Joan hasn’t finished the scope of change yet, so she should include the price of the printers. The scope of change says what the change covers, including its cost.
whyWrong: Risk analysis comes after the scope of the change is complete.
Training users comes after the change is approved and put in place.
The board needs the complete change document, including the scope, before it reviews it.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 28: Operational Procedures, Chapter Review question 3

stem: Once the change board has reviewed and approved Joan’s plan for the new printers, what’s her NEXT step?
options: Create a rollback plan in case the quality of print with the laser printers isn’t sufficient for the marketing materials.
explanation: Once the change board has approved the change plan, Joan should make sure to have a good rollback plan in place in case something unforeseen and negative happens. A rollback plan returns the systems to their earlier state if the change fails.
whyWrong: The rollback plan must exist before it can be tested.
Change documentation is finished before the board reviews it.
Implementing the change before a rollback plan exists is risky.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 28: Operational Procedures, Chapter Review question 4

stem: What broad term describes the process of enabling organizations to implement changes to IT infrastructure in a safe and cost-effective manner?
explanation: The term change management describes the process organizations use to implement changes to IT infrastructure in a safe and cost-effective manner. It includes request forms, risk analysis, board approval, implementation, and end-user acceptance.
whyWrong: Change documentation is part of change management, not the whole process.
Management documentation is not the term for the process of making safe changes.
Network documentation describes the network; it is not the change process.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 28: Operational Procedures, Chapter Review question 6

stem: As part of the change-management process, educating users on new systems is an important component in which of the following?
explanation: Training users in new or updated systems leads to end-user acceptance of the changes. Users who understand the new system are more likely to accept the change.
whyWrong: A rollback plan returns systems to the old state; it is not user education.
Accessibility training is not a step of change management.
Risk analysis looks at what could go wrong; it does not train users.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 28: Operational Procedures, Chapter Review question 7

stem: Which of the following is a detailed assessment of possible problems that could result from change?
explanation: A risk analysis is a detailed assessment of possible problems that could result from change. The risk analysis gives each change a risk level for the change board.
whyWrong: An acceptable use policy sets the rules for using company resources.
A new-user setup checklist lists the steps to onboard a new employee.
Regulatory requirements are laws and rules, not an assessment of a change.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 28: Operational Procedures, Chapter Review question 9

stem: Management within a banking organization is reviewing change management documentation. The team needs to understand the correct steps used within the process. When a change has been approved, what is the NEXT step?
explanation: Once a change request has been approved by the change advisory board, the next logical step in the change process is sandbox testing. This is performed during the testing phase to isolate the change in a controlled environment and assess its impact on system functionality and performance. Sandbox testing allows an organization to replicate a production environment.
whyWrong: End-user acceptance comes after the change has been put in place.
Risk analysis is done during planning, before the change is approved.
The book places stakeholder communication after sandbox testing in this process.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 2

stem: A bank must implement operational controls after recommendations were made by a third-party audit. The bank must implement change management best practices for all its information systems. The implementation team must understand what term is used to describe the range or boundaries of a change. Which of the following is the correct term?
explanation: The term that defines the extent or boundaries of a change is the scope. The scope outlines the specific objectives, deliverables, and limits of a change project or initiative. It helps define what is included and excluded within the scope of the change, ensuring a clear understanding and effective management of the project’s goals and boundaries.
whyWrong: Impact is the effect of a change, not its range or boundaries.
Purpose is the reason for a change, not its range or boundaries.
Analysis is the examination of information, not the boundaries of a change.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 69

stem: In a change management board meeting, you are discussing any vulnerabilities that can be mitigated as part of a recommended change and anything that could potentially occur due to that change. What BEST describes what you are discussing?
explanation: You are discussing risk analysis, which is the attempt to determine what threats could occur with computers and networks. The purpose of a change is a basic description of the change and why the change should come about. The scope of a change is to detail what systems will be updated. The backout plan is a set of procedures that will reverse any failed changes made quickly and efficiently. Documenting changes happens once approval is made; you should carefully document any changes that are made and when.
whyWrong: The purpose of the change is a basic description of the change and why it should happen.
The scope of the change details which systems the change will update.
A backout plan is a set of procedures that quickly reverses a failed change.
Documenting changes happens after approval and records what was changed and when.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: You have been tasked with backing up new user profiles in an enterprise environment. You propose to back up these user accounts to a new tape backup device. Which of the following procedures should you follow? (Select the two BEST answers.)
explanation: Because this is a change (backing up to a new tape device), a change management document will probably be needed, listing procedures for usage of the new backup device and the backup of the new accounts. Backup testing should be done often, or at least periodically, and definitely when it comes to new data, as is the case in this scenario with new user profiles.
whyWrong: The backup change should be transparent to users, so end-user acceptance is not a concern here.
Windows Backup is a desktop tool; an enterprise uses Windows Server Backup or a third-party product.
New user profiles need a full backup first, not an incremental backup of changes only.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: You work with servers and network infrastructure in an IT department. You are proposing a major operating system upgrade to a Linux server. You have completed the documentation for this, and it shows that the upgrade will impact your organization’s web services. You finish the required risk analysis and document the processes that will be required. Which of the following should you complete NEXT?
explanation: The technical assessments are finished, and you know how you would proceed with the process of upgrading the Linux server. Now it’s time to actually fill out the paperwork required by your organization. This would most likely be a change request form. This and any supporting documentation and assessments will be presented to a change control board or committee. It will hopefully include many things, such as the purpose of the change, the scope of the change, a rollback plan (or backout plan), systems affected, and so on.
whyWrong: A rollback plan is one part of the change request, not the next separate step to complete.
The purpose of the change is a section inside the change request form, not a separate next step.
The scope of the change is written into the change request; it is not completed on its own.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: Which of the following will bring a system back to its original state before a change was made? (Select the two BEST answers.)
explanation: A responsible staff member is the person (likely you) who will oversee the business process in question. The business process in question here is a rollback plan that will bring the system back to the original state before the change was made. Sandbox testing is a detailed procedure that explains how applications and systems will be tested in an isolated environment, which is often a virtual machine (VM). An undocumented business process is just that: a business process that has yet to be documented.
whyWrong: Sandbox testing tests applications and systems in an isolated environment; it does not undo a change.
An undocumented business process has not been written down yet, so it cannot restore a system.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods, Cram Quiz question 6
note: The book keys "A responsible staff member" as one of the answers because that person oversees the rollback plan. Book answer kept.

stem: You are executing the primary plan in the change management documentation and realize that you cannot proceed. Which section details the original configuration?
explanation: The rollback section contains the original configuration that can be used to revert the changes. The purpose section contains the reason for the proposed change. The risk analysis section explains the risks involved with the proposed changes. The plan for change section contains the primary change configuration and the alternate change configuration.
whyWrong: The purpose section gives the reason for the proposed change, not the original configuration.
The risk analysis section explains the risks of the change, not the original configuration.
The plan for change section holds the primary and alternate change configurations.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 2

stem: Which section of the change management documentation contains whom the change will affect?
explanation: The scope of change section details whom the change will affect. The business processes section details the current business processes the change will affect. The end-user acceptance section details how the changes were tested and accepted by the users. The plan for change contains the primary and alternate plans for the proposed change.
whyWrong: The business processes section lists current processes that the change affects, not the people.
The end-user acceptance section says how the change was tested and accepted by users.
The plan for change section holds the primary and alternate plans for the change.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 3

stem: A junior administrator was given a verbal warning by the IT manager following an incident where they patched the exchange server during working hours. This resulted in rebooting the server and 600 users not having access to their email for 15 minutes. Which of the following BEST describes the junior administrator’s actions?
explanation: The junior administrator has violated company policies. The standard operating procedure would state that any server updates should be done out of hours. They did not carry out patch management as that would be an enterprise solution. They just applied a single update to a single server.
whyWrong: Patch management is an enterprise process; applying one update to one server is not that process.
Not warning users was poor practice, but the main fault was breaking the rule on update timing.
Establishing a plan of action is a troubleshooting step, and there was no problem to troubleshoot.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.1 question 2
note: 220-1101 5.1 (troubleshooting methodology); mapped to 220-1202 4.2 (documented business processes and change management).

stem: A company is updating operational procedures and will adopt change management. Which of the following BEST describes a basic change-management best practice?
options: Communicating changes only after they have been implemented
explanation: Documenting changes thoroughly is a basic change-management best practice because it helps maintain a record of all modifications made, making it easier to track and troubleshoot issues if they arise. A documented record of each change also supports the change board review and makes a rollback easier.
whyWrong: Changes made without planning can cause unexpected outages because no one has assessed the risk or impact.
Users should hear about changes before they happen so they can prepare for any downtime.
User feedback helps confirm that a change works, so ignoring it leads to poor end-user acceptance.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.2 question 1

stem: Which of the following is a key element of change management?
explanation: Assessing and managing risks is a key element of change management. By identifying potential risks and implementing appropriate mitigation strategies, organizations can ensure a smoother transition during change implementation.
whyWrong: Users should be involved, because their feedback and acceptance are needed for a change to succeed.
Stakeholders must be kept informed so they can approve the change and prepare for its impact.
Rushing the implementation skips testing and review, which increases the chance of failures.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.2 question 2

stem: Which of the following is a recommended practice for managing user resistance during change implementation?
options: Limiting user access to system documentation
Implementing changes abruptly without prior notice
explanation: Providing clear communication and training is a recommended practice for managing user resistance during change implementation. By keeping users informed about the changes and their benefits, and by providing adequate training, organizations can address concerns and increase user acceptance.
whyWrong: Ignoring user concerns increases resistance and makes users less likely to accept the change.
Limiting access to documentation leaves users unsure how the new system works and adds to resistance.
Abrupt changes without notice surprise users and usually increase their resistance.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.2 question 3

stem: Which of the following BEST describes the purpose of a change advisory board (CAB)?
options: Monitoring the progress of change implementation
Limiting user involvement in the change process
explanation: The purpose of a change advisory board (CAB) is to evaluate and prioritize proposed changes. The CAB ensures that changes align with organizational goals, assesses their impact, and decides their priority for implementation.
whyWrong: A CAB reviews each change; approving everything without review defeats the purpose of the board.
Implementation progress is tracked by the change owner, while the CAB evaluates and approves changes beforehand.
The change process should include users; the CAB does not exist to limit their involvement.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.2 question 4

stem: Which of the following is a common risk associated with change management?
explanation: Temporary service disruptions are a common risk associated with change management. Implementing changes can sometimes result in system downtime or disruptions, affecting user productivity during the transition.
whyWrong: Improved system performance is a hoped-for benefit of a change, not a risk.
Increased user satisfaction is a goal of change management, not a risk it must manage.
Enhanced security is a benefit that a change can bring, not a risk of the change process.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.2 question 5

stem: Which of the following is an example of a change management best practice for software deployments?
explanation: Performing regular backups is an example of a change management best practice for software deployments. Backups ensure that data can be restored if there are any issues or failures during the deployment process.
whyWrong: Skipping testing lets faulty software reach production, so testing in a sandbox first is the best practice.
Changes are scheduled in maintenance windows outside peak hours to limit the impact on users.
Users should be told about a deployment beforehand so they can plan for it.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.2 question 6

stem: Which of the following is an example of a change management best practice for hardware replacements?
explanation: Conducting a thorough inventory assessment is an example of a change management best practice for hardware replacements. It ensures that organizations have accurate information about existing hardware, facilitating proper planning and decision-making during replacements.
whyWrong: User feedback reveals requirements for the new hardware, so ignoring it leads to poor planning.
Untested changes can fail in production, so hardware changes should be tested before rollout.
Stakeholders need to review and approve the change, so excluding them is poor practice.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.2 question 7

stem: Which of the following BEST describes the purpose of a rollback plan in change management?
options: Preventing any changes from being implemented
Documenting the reasons for change implementation
Identifying potential issues and their resolutions
Excluding user feedback during the change process
explanation: The purpose of a rollback plan in change management is to identify potential issues that may occur during the change implementation and outline the steps to revert back to the previous state if necessary. A rollback plan is the contingency that returns systems to their previous state when a change fails.
whyWrong: A rollback plan does not prevent changes; it provides a way back if a change causes problems.
The reasons for a change are recorded as its purpose on the change request form, not in the rollback plan.
User feedback is part of end-user acceptance, and a rollback plan does not exclude it.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.2 question 8

stem: Which of the following is a recommended practice for managing change-related risks?
explanation: Conducting regular risk assessments is a recommended practice for managing change-related risks. By periodically assessing potential risks associated with changes, organizations can proactively identify and mitigate them to minimize negative impacts.
whyWrong: Skipping risk assessment leaves potential problems unidentified until they cause damage.
A change without a backup plan cannot be safely undone if it fails.
Ignoring mitigation strategies leaves known risks in place and increases the chance of disruption.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.2 question 9

stem: Which of the following is a key consideration when communicating changes to users during change management?
options: Overemphasizing the negative aspects of the changes
Tailoring the message to the target audience
Delaying communication until after the changes are implemented
explanation: Tailoring the message to the target audience is a key consideration when communicating changes to users during change management. Different users may have varying levels of technical knowledge and concerns, so customizing the communication helps ensure their understanding and acceptance.
whyWrong: Vague information confuses users and leaves them unprepared for the change.
Focusing on the negative aspects increases user anxiety and resistance to the change.
Users need notice before a change, not only after it has been implemented.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.2 question 10

stem: A technician wants to upgrade the operating system on a web server. The technician has documented the purpose and scope of the change, tested it in a sandbox, and completed the risk analysis. What should the technician do NEXT?
options: Submit a change request form to the change advisory board
Install the upgrade on the production server
Ask end users to accept the change
Close the change in the documentation
explanation: With the planning and testing done, the change must be put on a request form and presented to the change advisory board. Only an approved change may be carried out on the production server.
whyWrong: Making the change before it is approved is an unauthorized change, even when the testing went well.
End-user acceptance comes after the change is approved and made, not before the request is submitted.
The change cannot be closed before it has been approved, made, and accepted.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

stem: A retail company's point-of-sale system stops working on a Saturday afternoon because of a critical flaw, and stores cannot take payments. A vendor fix is available now. Which change type will MOST LIKELY be used to install it?
explanation: An emergency change is a high-priority change made at once to fix a critical problem that disrupts the business. Its review and approval are expedited so that normal operations return quickly.
whyWrong: A standard change is a pre-approved, low-risk routine change, not an urgent fix for a critical outage.
A normal change goes through the full review and approval cycle, which is too slow for a critical outage.
A change freeze is a period when changes are blocked; it is not a type of change.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

stem: A network administrator plans a firmware upgrade on the core switch. The change advisory board asks how the network will be returned to its current state if the upgrade fails. Which part of the change plan BEST answers this question?
explanation: A rollback plan, also called a backout plan, lists the steps to return to the original state when a change fails. It usually includes the saved original configuration and the steps to restore it.
whyWrong: The purpose of the change says why the change is needed, not how to undo it.
End-user acceptance confirms that users agree the change works; it does not reverse a failed change.
A peer review checks a change for effects on other departments; it does not restore the old state.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

stem: Joan is looking for the quickest way to take very frequent backups of an important database. Which of the following media would be BEST?
explanation: Joan should check out solid-state drives, which offer more speed in exchange for a higher price. The trade-off is cost, because SSDs cost more per gigabyte than hard drives or tape.
whyWrong: Cloud storage depends on the Internet connection, which is slower than a local SSD.
Magnetic tape is cheap for large archives but slow for frequent backups.
Magnetic hard drives are cheaper per gigabyte but slower than solid-state drives.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 14: Maintaining and Optimizing Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 8
note: 220-1102 4.3; backup media are not listed under 220-1202 4.3, mapped to 220-1202 4.3 (backup).

stem: What Windows feature enables you to back up your important files and folders regularly?
explanation: File History enables you to perform backups of important files and folders regularly. File History copies the files in the user's libraries to another drive on a schedule.
whyWrong: Time Machine is the macOS backup feature, not a Windows one.
Backup and Restore is the older Windows 7 tool, not the current feature for regular file backups.
System Snapshot is not a Windows feature.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 14: Maintaining and Optimizing Operating Systems, Chapter Review question 10

stem:
Your security team needs to satisfy the following requirements of a disaster recovery plan:

- The last month of backups should be easily accessible and preferably on-premises.

- Long-term backups should be stored offsite.

- There should be minimal use of hardware.

Which of the following answers will BEST meet the requirements?
options: Store backups with a cloud provider and onsite.
Store 30 days’ worth of backups onsite and store anything older than that with an offsite cloud provider.
Store all backups with a cloud provider.
Store backups onsite and use cloud bursting if the backup hardware demands more resources.
explanation: Store 30 days (1 month) of backups onsite (on-premises, or “on-prem”) and store older backups with a cloud provider that is offsite (and preferably in a different geographic location). This meets all the requirements in the question: The last month of backups is easily accessible; the reason is that it is onsite, long-term backups are stored offsite (cloud provider), and there is minimal use of hardware because you don’t have to use as many tapes, disk arrays, and NAS boxes since the cloud is storing all backups older than 30 days. Of course, the cloud provider will use a lot of hardware, and that’s part of the point of using the cloud. All that said, it’s a good idea to have your 30 days of on-premises backups duplicated and stored offsite as well. Remember the 3-2-1 rule?
whyWrong: Storing backups both in the cloud and onsite does not say which backups go where.
Storing everything in the cloud breaks the rule that recent backups stay on-premises.
Cloud bursting adds resources for heavy workloads and still needs a lot of local backup hardware.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 16

stem: Important business data must be backed up to meet industry regulations, a technician is seeking the most suitable backup method. The requirement is to regularly modify only a few files while considering limited storage space. Which backup methods should the technician choose?
explanation: To address the concerns of regularly modifying only a few files and limited storage space while meeting regulatory requirements, the most effective backup method is incremental backup. Incremental backups only store the changes made since the last full or incremental backup, resulting in smaller backup sizes and quicker backup operations. This approach optimizes storage space utilization and reduces the time required for backup operations.
whyWrong: A full backup copies every file each time and uses the most storage.
Cloud backup is about where the copy is stored, not about saving space for a few changed files.
Tape rotation is about how media are reused, not about saving storage.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 13

stem: A technician, working for a large regional bank, is configuring a new tape backup system. After installing the system in the server room, which backup types will need to be completed FIRST?
explanation: When implementing a new backup system, the initial backup that should be performed is a complete or full backup. A complete backup copies all data and files from the source system to the backup storage medium. This comprehensive backup captures the entire system and establishes a baseline for future backups. The full backup will clear the archive bit on all files, indicating that they have backed up.
whyWrong: A copy backup copies all files but does not set the baseline by clearing the archive bit.
Mirror backup is not one of the standard backup types.
A differential backup needs an earlier full backup as its baseline.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 16

stem: Given the Chief Financial Officer’s concerns about maintaining access to sensitive, legacy, unmaintained personally identifiable information (PII) on a workstation in the event of a ransomware outbreak, and considering the regulatory requirement to retain this data for an extended period, which of the following backup methods would be the MOST suitable?
options: Daily, incremental backup that is securely stored on an external hard drive
Regular snapshots taken and stored on a network-attached storage ( NAS) device
A complete backup of the data that is transferred to an offline, encrypted tape storage
Weekly, differential backups that are securely transmitted to an offsite backup service
explanation: Given the concerns regarding sensitive, legacy, unmaintained PII and the regulatory requirement for long-term data retention, the best approach would be to perform a complete backup of the data. Storing this backup on an offline, encrypted tape storage ensures that the data remains secure and protected from ransomware attacks. The transfer of data to offline storage provides an added layer of protection against potential data loss.
whyWrong: An external drive that stays connected can be encrypted by ransomware, and incrementals depend on other backups.
Snapshots on a NAS can be reached by ransomware if the NAS is compromised.
Differential backups depend on an earlier full backup and are not a complete long-term copy.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 44

stem: Which type of backup scheme uses two types of media, with one being stored offsite?
explanation: The 3-2-1 rule is a backup scheme that specifies three copies of data: one in use and two others that are stored on different media types, with one of those being stored offsite. The grandfather-father-son (GFS) backup scheme uses three sets of backup tapes: daily, weekly, and monthly. The 10-tape rotation uses two weeks’ worth of daily tapes, which are reused after a two-week period. Cloud storage is a possible backup scheme for your data, and although it is offsite, it does not deal with different types of media.
whyWrong: GFS uses three sets of backup tapes (daily, weekly, and monthly), not a rule about media types.
The 10-tape rotation reuses two weeks of daily tapes and says nothing about different media or offsite copies.
Cloud storage is offsite, but on its own it is not a scheme that uses two types of media.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: You have implemented a backup solution that combines a full backup on Monday at 6 p.m. and incremental backups on Tuesday through Friday at 6 p.m. If there was a storage drive failure on Saturday morning, how many backup tapes would be required to restore the entire backup?
explanation: You would need all five backup tapes to restore the entire backup. That would include the full backup from Monday, and the four incremental backup tapes from Tuesday through Friday. If you had also set up a synthetic backup on Saturday, then you would need only that one tape. If perhaps the failure occurred on Friday morning instead of Saturday, then you would need only four tapes: the full backup and the three incremental tapes from Tuesday through Thursday.
whyWrong: One tape would be enough only with a synthetic full backup made after the last incremental.
Two tapes would be enough only with a full backup plus one differential backup.
Four tapes would be enough only if the failure had happened on Friday morning, before Friday's backup.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: Which type of backup allows users to restore their own files without IT intervention?
explanation: Volume Shadow Copy allows users to restore previous versions of their files themselves. Image-based restoration typically requires a desktop administrator. Incremental and differential backup and restores also require IT intervention for restoration.
whyWrong: Restoring from an image-based backup usually needs a desktop administrator.
Restoring from an incremental backup needs IT to run the restore.
Restoring from a differential backup needs IT to run the restore.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 5
note: Volume Shadow Copy (previous versions) is not named in 220-1202 4.3; mapped to 4.3 recovery.

stem: Which backup media is the fastest from which to recover?
explanation: Disk-to-disk is the fastest recovery method and backup method as well, because you are backing up from a disk to another disk attached via the network. Disk-to-tape is slower because you must re-tension the tape and then locate the data on the tape to recover it. Disk-to-flash is not a backup method, because of the price of flash. Disk-to-cloud is the slowest recovery method because you must recover from the cloud over a network connection.
whyWrong: Tape is slower to recover from because the tape must be tensioned and searched for the data.
The book says disk-to-flash is not a backup method because flash storage is too expensive.
The cloud is the slowest to recover from because the data comes back over a network connection.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 8
note: Backup media speed is not a named 220-1202 sub-topic; mapped to 4.3 recovery.

stem: You need to upgrade a server and want to make a backup of the data before you begin. Which backup method should you choose so that your normal backups are not affected?
explanation: You should use the copy backup method, since it will perform a full backup of the files without resetting the archive bits. A full backup makes a full backup and resets all the archive bits affecting the normal backups. Because the archive bits are left as they are, the next scheduled backup runs as if the copy never happened.
whyWrong: A full backup resets the archive bits, which affects the normal backup schedule.
An incremental backup resets the archive bits of the files it copies, which affects later backups.
A differential backup copies only the changed files, so it is not a complete copy of the data.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 9
note: The book's explanation has the archive bit behavior of incremental and differential backups reversed (an incremental backup resets the bits; a differential backup does not); those sentences are left out. The copy backup is not named in 220-1202 4.3.

stem: Which workstation backup method involves creating a copy of all user data and settings at a specific point in time?
explanation: A full backup creates a complete copy of all data and settings, providing a comprehensive snapshot of the workstation at that particular moment. This method allows for a complete restoration in case of data loss.
whyWrong: A differential backup copies only the data changed since the last full backup, not all data.
An incremental backup copies only the data changed since the last backup of any type.
A selective backup copies only the files or folders a user chooses, not all data and settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.3 question 1

stem: Which workstation recovery method involves using a backup of the entire workstation’s hard drive to restore the system to its previous state?
explanation: Bare-metal recovery involves restoring an entire workstation’s operating system, applications, and data from a complete backup, often in situations where the system needs to be rebuilt from scratch or migrated to new hardware. It is used when the original system cannot start or when the restore goes to new hardware.
whyWrong: Cloud-based recovery describes where backups are stored, not a restore of the entire drive.
File-level recovery restores individual files or folders, not the whole system.
Incremental recovery restores a chain of changed data and is not a full system restore method.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.3 question 2
note: 220-1102 4.3; bare-metal recovery is not named in 220-1202 4.3, mapped to 4.3 (recovery)

stem: Which backup storage medium provides the fastest transfer rates but is also the most expensive option for workstation backup?
explanation: Tape drives offer fast transfer rates compared to other backup storage media, but they tend to be costly compared to other options. Tape drives write data sequentially at high speed, which suits large scheduled backups.
whyWrong: External hard drives are a popular, low-cost choice, but the book rates their transfer rate below tape.
Network-attached storage is convenient, but its speed is limited by the network connection.
Cloud storage is easy to scale, but internet bandwidth makes its transfer rates slower for large backups.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.3 question 3
note: 220-1102 4.3; mapped to 220-1202 4.3 (backup). For one workstation, a tape drive costs far more than the other options, and current LTO drives have a higher sustained write rate than one external drive, a gigabit NAS link, or a cloud upload; tape media itself is cheap per gigabyte.

stem: Which workstation backup method only backs up data that has changed since the last backup, regardless of whether it was a full or incremental backup?
explanation: An incremental backup is designed to only back up data that has changed since the last backup. This type of backup is designed to reduce backup time and requires less storage space.
whyWrong: A differential backup copies everything changed since the last full backup and ignores earlier incremental backups.
A synthetic full backup combines a full backup and later incremental backups into a new full backup.
Continuous backup copies changes in real time as they happen rather than at each scheduled backup.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.3 question 4

stem: Which backup rotation scheme involves using a set of backup media and cycling through them on a daily basis, overwriting the oldest backup when the set is full?
explanation: The grandfather-father-son rotation scheme involves using a set of backup media and cycling through them on a daily basis. The oldest backup is overwritten when the set becomes full. This scheme provides a combination of daily, weekly, and monthly backups.
whyWrong: Tower of Hanoi is a rotation scheme with a more complex pattern than simple daily cycling.
Back up to disk names a backup target, not a scheme for rotating backup media.
Back up to tape names a type of backup media, not a rotation scheme.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.3 question 5

stem: Which workstation backup method provides the fastest recovery time when compared to other backup methods?
explanation: Snapshot backup provides the fastest recovery time when compared to other backup methods. Snapshots capture the state of the workstation’s system and data at a specific point in time, allowing for quick restoration to that exact state.
whyWrong: An incremental restore needs the last full backup plus every later incremental backup, which takes longer.
A differential restore needs the last full backup plus the latest differential backup, which takes longer than a snapshot.
A full backup restore copies all the data back, which is slower than reverting to a snapshot.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.3 question 6
note: 220-1102 4.3; snapshots are not named in 220-1202 4.3, mapped to 4.3 (recovery)

stem: Which backup method ensures data redundancy by creating multiple copies of backups on different backup media?
explanation: Mirroring ensures data redundancy by creating identical copies of backups on different backup media simultaneously. This method enhances data availability and fault tolerance.
whyWrong: Replication copies data to other systems or locations rather than writing backups to several media at once.
Archiving moves inactive data to long-term storage for retention, not to make redundant backup copies.
Versioning keeps several versions of a file over time but does not create copies on separate media.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.3 question 7
note: 220-1102 4.3; mirroring is not named in 220-1202 4.3, mapped to 4.3 (backup)

stem: Which backup method provides the highest level of data protection by storing multiple copies of backups across different geographical locations?
explanation: Offsite backup involves storing backups in a location outside the primary site, providing protection against disasters or physical damage that could affect the original location. By storing backups in different geographical locations, data is safeguarded against localized events.
whyWrong: Cloud backup stores data remotely but does not by itself guarantee copies in several geographic locations.
Tape backup names a type of media; tapes kept at the main site give no protection from local disasters.
Disk-to-disk backup copies data to another disk, which is often at the same site as the original.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.3 question 8

stem: Which workstation backup method captures an exact copy of the workstation’s operating system, applications, and data, allowing for quick restoration to a functional state?
explanation: Image backup captures an exact copy of the workstation’s operating system, applications, and data, allowing for quick restoration to a functional state. It creates a snapshot of the entire workstation’s configuration.
whyWrong: File-level backup copies selected files and folders, not the operating system and applications.
An incremental backup copies only the data changed since the last backup, not an exact copy of the system.
A differential backup copies only the data changed since the last full backup, not the whole system.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.3 question 9
note: 220-1102 4.3; image backups are not named in 220-1202 4.3, mapped to 4.3 (backup)

stem: Which workstation backup method involves automatically backing up data in real time as changes occur, ensuring minimal data loss in the event of a failure?
explanation: Continuous backup involves automatically backing up data in real time as changes occur. This method ensures minimal data loss in the event of a failure, as the backups are kept up to date at all times.
whyWrong: Synchronization keeps copies the same in different places but does not necessarily back up in real time.
A manual backup runs only when a user starts it, so it can miss recent changes.
A snapshot captures the system at one point in time rather than recording every change as it occurs.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.3 question 10
note: 220-1102 4.3; continuous backup is not named in 220-1202 4.3, mapped to 4.3 (backup)

stem: A small office runs a full backup every Sunday night. The weeknight backup window is short, but the manager wants any restore to need no more than two backup sets. Which backup type is the BEST choice for the weeknights?
explanation: A differential backup copies everything changed since the last full backup and does not clear the archive bit. A restore then needs only the Sunday full backup and the latest differential.
whyWrong: Incremental backups are fast, but a restore needs the full backup and every incremental since, which can be more than two sets.
A full backup every night needs the longest backup window, which the office does not have.
A copy backup copies everything like a full backup, so it is too slow for a short weeknight window.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

stem: A company's backup software has reported a successful job every night for a year. The IT manager realizes that nobody has ever restored data from these backups. Which action is BEST?
options: Restore selected backup jobs to a test system on a regular schedule and compare the data
Switch to a differential backup type
Move all backup media to an offsite vault
Turn on the software's write verification and stop there
explanation: A backup is not proven until data has been restored from it successfully. Regular test restores to a test system, at least monthly, show that the backups really work.
whyWrong: Changing the backup type does not prove that the existing or new backups can be restored.
Moving media offsite protects against a site disaster, but it does not show whether the backups can be read.
