Write verification checks that the job was written, but it is not enough without real test restores.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

stem: A clinic keeps its patient records on a server and backs them up nightly to a NAS in the same room. The owner wants protection if a fire destroys the building. Which change BEST meets this need?
options: Follow the 3-2-1 rule by adding a second backup on another kind of media that is kept offsite
Change the nightly backups from incremental to full
Add a second NAS in the same server room
Run a test restore once a year
explanation: The 3-2-1 rule keeps three copies of the data on two kinds of media, with one copy offsite. The offsite copy survives a disaster that destroys the building and every onsite copy.
whyWrong: Full backups still sit on the same NAS in the same room, so a fire would destroy them too.
A second NAS in the same room is still onsite and would be lost in the same fire.
Test restores prove the backups work, but they do not protect the data from a fire at the site.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

stem: At the very least, what tool should be in every technician’s toolkit?
explanation: Every tech’s toolkit should have a Phillips-head screwdriver, at the very least. Most screws in desktop and laptop computers are Phillips-head, so this one screwdriver handles most jobs.
whyWrong: Pliers are handy, but most screws in a PC need a screwdriver, not pliers.
A hammer has no place in PC repair and can damage components.
Straight-slot screws are rare in PCs; most computer screws are Phillips-head.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 1: Safety and Professionalism, Chapter Review question 3
note: 220-1102 4.4; toolkits are not a 220-1202 topic, mapped to 220-1202 4.4 (proper component handling).

stem: Which tool helps you avoid accidental static discharge by keeping you at the same electrical potential as the computer on which you’re working?
explanation: An ESD wrist strap keeps you at the same electrical potential as the computer. The strap's clip attaches to the computer case so that you and the computer share the same electrical potential.
whyWrong: Antistatic spray reduces static on carpets and surfaces; it does not connect you to the computer.
An antistatic bag protects a component in storage; it does not keep you at the computer's potential.
A Phillips-head screwdriver removes screws; it gives no protection against static discharge.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 1: Safety and Professionalism, Chapter Review question 8

stem: You have been asked to set up a new networking closet, and you notice that the humidity level in the room is very low. Which of the following tasks should be done before rack-mounting any networking equipment?
explanation: All networking racks should be grounded, either to grounding bars or an I-beam in the ceiling or using some other grounding method. This should be done before installing any equipment to the racks to prevent any damage from electrostatic discharge (ESD).
whyWrong: A dehumidifier would lower the humidity further and increase the risk of ESD.
An ESD strap protects devices only while you work on them, not after you disconnect.
Fire suppression is important, but it does not protect equipment from ESD.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 17

stem: Which type of fire extinguishing technology should be used during an electrical fire?
explanation: Non-water-based fire extinguishers should be used during an electrical fire. This could be a CO2-based fire extinguisher such as a Class C extinguisher, a Halotron fire extinguisher, or an FM-200 overhead system.
whyWrong: Overhead sprinklers use water and should not be near expensive computer equipment.
Water-based extinguishers conduct electricity and must not be used on electrical fires.
Class B extinguishers are for burning gases and liquids; electrical fires need Class C.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 43

stem: You are required to replace a desktop power supply. Which of the following tasks should be performed FIRST?
options: Review local regulations for disposal procedures.
explanation: Remove watches, jewelry, and any other metals when working on a computer so they are out of the way and do not pose any threats while working on the computer. Metal jewelry can conduct electricity and catch on components inside the case.
whyWrong: Disposal rules matter when you get rid of the old part, not before you start.
The MSDS is for chemicals and spills, not for replacing a power supply.
Environmental concerns apply to disposal, not to the first step of the repair.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 51
note: 220-1202 4.4 lists electrical and personal safety; removing jewelry fits personal safety.

stem: When you are handling internal computer components, which are best practices to avoid ESD? (Select the two best answers.)
options: Ground yourself before touching the components.
Verify that the device is plugged into a grounded outlet.
Handle adapter cards by the edge.
explanation: First, ground yourself. The best way is to use an antistatic strap and other antistatic measures, including touching the chassis of the computer. Second, handle adapter cards and other electronics by the edge to avoid making contact with any of the circuitry—but don’t touch the slot connectors!
whyWrong: A dry environment increases static, so humidity should be kept higher.
The device should be unplugged while you work on it.
Eye protection is for hazardous materials, not a measure against ESD.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 88

stem: Several desktop computers are to be upgraded in order to support a new software installation. The system upgrades will involve replacing the processor and increasing the memory in the desktop computers. Which of the following should be done to ensure no damage occurs during this upgrade process?
options: Ground yourself by using an anti-static wrist strap before handling any components
Upgrade the processor first, then add the memory modules afterward
Keep the computers powered on while making the upgrades
Skip the anti-static precautions as they are not necessary for desktop upgrades
explanation: When working on internal computer components like processors and memory modules, it’s crucial to prevent electrostatic discharge (ESD), which can damage sensitive electronic parts. Using an anti-static wrist strap helps to discharge any static electricity from your body, protecting the components.
whyWrong: The order of the upgrades does not prevent damage from static.
Computers must be powered off and unplugged before you change parts.
Anti-static precautions are needed for desktops as much as for any electronics.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 33

stem: If a power supply fails, what should you do?
options: Switch it to a different voltage setting.
explanation: Replace the power supply. Trying to repair it can be dangerous and is not cost-effective to the company. Power supplies hold high voltage in their capacitors even after they are unplugged, so they are treated as field-replaceable units and are not opened.
whyWrong: Opening a power supply to repair it is dangerous because of stored charge, and it is not cost-effective.
Moving to a different computer avoids the problem but does not fix the failed power supply.
Changing the voltage setting does not fix a failed power supply and can damage the computer.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Which of the following are ways to avoid ESD? (Select all that apply.)
options: Touch the chassis of the computer.
explanation: Using antistatic wrist straps and mats and touching the chassis (self-grounding) of the computer are all ways to stop ESD. Vacuum cleaners can cause damage to components.
whyWrong: A vacuum cleaner can build up static and damage components, so it is not a way to avoid ESD.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: You walk into the server room and see a person lying on the floor with a live electrical wire draped over. Which two of the following should you do and in which order?
options: Grab the wire and fling it off the person.
Grab and drag the person out from under the wire.
Grab a piece of wood and use it to move the wire off the person.
explanation: The first thing to do is call 911 and get emergency help on the way. After that, if emergency dispatchers approve, you should get a wooden stick, rope, or something similar (every server room should have one) and use it to CAREFULLY move the wire off of the person. In reality, the first thing you should do is breathe and not make any rash decisions in the heat of the moment. After the wire is removed, attempt to offer first aid to the victim. DO NOT ever touch a live wire or anything that the live wire is coming into contact with.
whyWrong: Touching a live wire with your hands can electrocute you, so never grab the wire.
Touching the person while the wire is on them can pass the current through you as well.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures, Cram Quiz question 3
note: The stem asks for two actions in order; the book's order is call 911 first, then move the wire with a piece of wood.

stem: A customer is “cleaning house” and asks you what to do with several older CRT monitors. What should you tell this customer?
options: Throw them in the dumpster out back.
Donate them to a thrift store.
Recycle them in compliance with local government regulations and/or municipal ordinances.
explanation: Electronic equipment and devices should be recycled in compliance with local government regulations and/or municipal ordinances. Electronic equipment and devices should never just be thrown away in public trash. They are considered e-waste—which is bad for the environment, and your customer could get fined or fired for not following company policy or local government regulations. You should never work inside CRT monitors. Due to the high voltage they carry, the potential for electrical shock if handled improperly, the heavy lead content in their construction, and the risk of glass shards if the screen is broken, proper handling and disposal are crucial.
whyWrong: Electronic devices are e-waste and must never go in public trash, which can bring fines.
CRT monitors carry dangerous high voltage, so a technician should not open or repair them.
Donating old CRT monitors only passes the disposal problem on; they must be recycled under local rules.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: You have dropped a screw into a tight location of a computer. How should you retrieve it?
options: Shake the computer until it falls out.
explanation: A three-pronged grabber should be used to retrieve the screw from the computer. Using a magnetic-tipped screwdriver is not advisable, because many components are sensitive to magnets. Using a magnetic grabber is not advisable, because many components are sensitive to magnets. Shaking the computer until it falls out can be dangerous and make the screw harder to get out.
whyWrong: Magnetic tools are not advised inside a computer because many components are sensitive to magnets.
A magnetic grabber is not advised because many computer components are sensitive to magnets.
Shaking the computer is risky and can move the screw to a place that is harder to reach.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns, Review Questions question 1
note: Tool use inside the case is mapped to 220-1202 4.4 proper component handling.

stem: What is the approximate minimum level of static charge for humans to feel a shock?
explanation: You can feel an ESD shock of 3,000 volts or more. 300 volts is too low for a human to feel. 300,000 volts can be felt by humans and could be painful. Components can be damaged by much smaller charges that a person never feels.
whyWrong: A charge of 300 volts is too low for a person to feel, although it can still damage components.
People can feel a shock well below 30,000 volts; about 3,000 volts is the usual threshold.
A person can feel 300,000 volts, but that is far above the minimum level for feeling a shock.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns, Review Questions question 6
note: The book's explanation also says that a minimum of 30,000 volts can be felt, which contradicts its key and its chapter (about 3,000 volts); that sentence is left out.

stem: Your work environment has been unusually dry lately, and several components have been damaged by ESD. Your team has been asked to be extra careful about ESD damage. Which of the following measures can be implemented to reduce the risk of ESD? (Choose two.)
explanation: Using an antistatic wrist strap allows you to ground yourself to dissipate a static charge. Using antistatic bags allows for a uniform charge around a component. Spraying disinfectant spray will only kill germs, not reduce static. Shuffling your feet will build a charge of static.
whyWrong: Disinfectant spray only kills germs and does nothing to reduce static.
Shuffling your feet builds up a static charge instead of removing it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns, Review Questions question 7

stem: Which of the following are OSHA requirements for a safe work environment that must be followed by employers? (Choose two.)
options: Attend yearly OSHA safe work environment seminars.
Provide properly maintained tools and equipment.
Have an OSHA employee stationed within 5 miles of the facility.
Display an OSHA poster in a prominent location.
explanation: Providing properly maintained tools and equipment is a requirement for an OSHA-compliant workplace. Displaying an OSHA poster in a prominent location is also a requirement for an OSHA-compliant workplace. Attending yearly OSHA safe work environment seminars is not a requirement. Having an OSHA employee stationed within five miles of the facility is also not a requirement.
whyWrong: OSHA does not require employers to attend yearly safe work environment seminars.
OSHA does not station an employee within a set distance of each facility.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns, Review Questions question 8

stem: Your office is moving from one floor of a building to another, and you are part of the moving crew. When moving computer equipment, which of the following are good procedures to follow? (Choose two.)
options: Lift by bending over at the waist.
Carry CRT monitors with the glass face away from your body.
Use a cart for heavy objects.
Ensure that there are no safety hazards in your path.
explanation: You should use a cart to move heavy objects. You should also ensure that no safety hazards are in your path. Lifting by bending over at the waist can hurt your back. Carrying CRT monitors with the glass facing outward is not safe, as the weight will be farthest from your body.
whyWrong: Bending over at the waist to lift can hurt your back; lift with your legs instead.
Carrying a CRT with the glass face away puts the heaviest part farthest from your body.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns, Review Questions question 10

stem: Which class of fire extinguisher is recommended for use in a wood and paper fire?
explanation: Wood and paper fires can be put out by a Class A fire extinguisher. Class B fire extinguishers are used for flammable liquids. Class C fire extinguishers are used for electrical fires. Class D fire extinguishers are used for flammable metals.
whyWrong: Class B fire extinguishers are for flammable liquids, not wood and paper.
Class C fire extinguishers are for electrical fires, not ordinary wood and paper.
Class D fire extinguishers are for flammable metals, not wood and paper.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns, Review Questions question 14
note: The book's explanation says "electrical files"; corrected to "electrical fires".

stem: Which of the following are common types of screwdrivers? (Choose two.)
explanation: Phillips and Torx are two common types of screwdrivers. Neither circular nor helix is a type of screwdriver. A technician's toolkit usually has several sizes of each of these.
whyWrong: Circular is not a type of screwdriver tip.
Helix is not a type of screwdriver tip.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns, Review Questions question 15
note: Tool kit contents are background; mapped to 220-1202 4.4 proper component handling.

stem: Which of the following are elements of a good workplace safety plan? (Choose two.)
options: A safety and health training program
Retribution for employees who report violations
An independent third-party auditor of the safety plan
explanation: Good safety plans protect the interests of the workers and also help to keep company costs down. Periodic workplace inspections and a training program are good components to implement. Employees cannot be punished in any way for reporting safety violations. Third-party audits of safety programs are not necessary but can complement periodic inspections and safety and health training programs.
whyWrong: Employees cannot be punished in any way for reporting safety violations.
A third-party auditor is not needed, although one can complement inspections and training.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns, Review Questions question 16

stem: What is the recommended use policy on magnetic-tipped screwdrivers inside computers?
options: It's okay to use them, but keep them away from the processor.
It's okay to use them, but keep them away from the RAM.
It's okay to use them, but only if they're of the powered variety.
explanation: A good rule of thumb when it comes to magnetic-tipped screwdrivers is to avoid using them inside a computer case. Magnetic tools can damage data on disks that use a magnetic storage scheme. Magnetic-tipped screwdrivers should not be used inside a computer even if they are kept away from the processor and the RAM. Regardless of whether they are powered or not, magnetic-tipped screwdrivers should not be used inside computers.
whyWrong: Magnetic-tipped screwdrivers should not be used inside the case even away from the processor.
Magnetic-tipped screwdrivers should not be used inside the case even away from the RAM.
Powered or not, magnetic-tipped screwdrivers should not be used inside a computer.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns, Review Questions question 17

stem: Which of the following are OSHA requirements for a safe work environment that must be followed by employees? (Choose two.)
options: Immediately report all accidents to OSHA.
Follow all employer-implemented health and safety rules.
explanation: To maintain a safe work environment, all employees must follow certain protocols. These include using protective gear and equipment and following all health and safety rules. Accidents must be reported to the employer, not OSHA (unless action is not properly taken by the employer). There are no rules requiring safety training, although it is a good idea to have these sessions and for employees to attend them.
whyWrong: Employees report accidents to the employer, not to OSHA, unless the employer does not act.
No OSHA rule makes employees attend safety training, although attending is a good idea.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns, Review Questions question 19

stem: What safety precautions should I take when replacing Random Access Memory (RAM) on Windows Server 2022? (Choose two.)
options: Put the machine in standby mode
Wear an electromagnetic static wrist strap
explanation: When replacing RAM, you should always power down the server and wear an electromagnetic static wrist strap. This will prevent you from damaging the RAM. Putting a machine in standby mode or trying to hot-swap RAM is not a good idea, as either could damage the RAM.
whyWrong: RAM is not hot-swappable in a normal server, and removing it under power can damage it.
Standby mode still powers the memory, so changing RAM in standby can damage it.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.2 question 1
note: 220-1101 5.2 (hardware troubleshooting); mapped to 220-1202 4.4 (ESD straps and disconnecting power). Book wording 'electromagnetic static wrist strap' kept; it means an ESD strap.

stem: How does a grounded ESD mat protect computer parts on a workbench?
options: It drains static charge away from items that touch it
It stores a static charge that later powers the parts
It insulates the parts from the technician's hands
It blocks electromagnetic interference from nearby devices
explanation: An ESD mat is connected to ground and drains excess charge from anything that touches it. When the technician's wrist strap is connected to the mat, the technician and the equipment are at the same electrical potential. With no difference in charge, no static discharge can damage the parts.
whyWrong: The mat removes static charge; it does not store charge or supply power to parts.
The mat does not insulate; it is slightly conductive so the charge can drain to ground.
An ESD mat controls static charge and is not a shield against electromagnetic interference.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

stem: A technician must run a power cable and a network cable across a busy hallway for a two-week event. Which method BEST keeps the cables from being a trip hazard and from being crushed?
options: Lay the cables in a floor cable guard
Tape the cables to the floor with gaffing tape
Run the cables under a loose rug
Coil the extra length in the middle of the hallway
explanation: When a cable must cross a trafficked area, a floor cable guard holds it in place and protects it from being crushed. The guard also gives people a low, visible surface to step over. Running cables through drop ceilings or conduits is better still when that is possible.
whyWrong: Gaffing tape is only a quick temporary fix and does not protect the cables from crushing.
A rug hides the cables, so people still trip on the bump and the cables can be crushed.
A coil of cable in a walkway creates a larger trip hazard, not a smaller one.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

stem: Which TWO statements about antistatic bags are true? (Choose two.)
options: Static charges collect on the outside of the bag instead of on the part inside
A part should stay in its bag until the technician is ready to install it
The bag drains charges to ground, so it can replace an antistatic mat
The bag should be kept off the antistatic mat so the two do not share a charge
explanation: Antistatic bags have a slightly conductive surface, so static charges collect on the outside rather than on the part inside. Parts such as adapter cards should stay in their bags until the technician is ready to install them. The bags do not drain charge, so they are used together with an antistatic mat, not in place of one.
whyWrong: Antistatic bags do not drain charges to ground, so they must not be used in place of a mat.
Keeping the bag on top of the antistatic mat is recommended, because the mat drains any charge.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

stem: Which of the following is a common safety procedure when working on computer hardware?
options: Disconnect the power supply without turning it off
Handle circuit boards with bare hands
explanation: Wearing an ESD (electrostatic discharge) wrist strap helps prevent static electricity from damaging computer components. It safely discharges any static electricity built up on your body.
whyWrong: Pulling the power without shutting down can corrupt data, and the system should be shut down first.
Handling circuit boards with bare hands can pass static and skin oils to the components.
Standing on a wet surface increases the risk of electric shock and slipping.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.4 question 1

stem: Which of the following safety measures should be followed when handling computer cables?
options: Pull the cable from a distance to disconnect it
Bend the cable sharply to fit it in tight spaces
Secure cables using cable ties or clips
explanation: Securing cables using cable ties or clips helps maintain an organized and tidy workspace, prevents tripping hazards, and protects the cables from damage due to pulling or tangling. Good cable management also keeps airflow clear inside and around equipment.
whyWrong: Pulling a cable from a distance strains the connector and can damage it; grip the connector instead.
Sharp bends can break the conductors inside a cable or damage its connector.
Loose, tangled cables create tripping hazards and are easily damaged.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.4 question 3

stem: What safety precaution should be taken before opening a computer case?
options: Ensure the computer is turned off and unplugged
Wear gloves to protect against static electricity
Use a metal tool to open the case
Keep the case on a soft, cushioned surface
explanation: Before opening a computer case, it is crucial to ensure the computer is turned off and unplugged. This eliminates the risk of electrical shock and protects both the technician and the hardware.
whyWrong: Ordinary gloves do not prevent static discharge, and an ESD strap is the correct protection.
A metal tool can short live components and is not a safety precaution for opening a case.
A soft, cushioned surface can build static and is not a safe work surface for a computer.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.4 question 4

stem: What should be done to prevent injuries while working with computer hardware?
options: Use damaged tools if no others are available
Skip breaks and work for long periods without rest
explanation: Following ergonomic practices, such as maintaining proper posture, using adjustable furniture, and taking regular breaks, helps prevent injuries such as musculoskeletal disorders and eye strain. Good posture, adjustable furniture, and regular breaks reduce strain during long repair sessions.
whyWrong: Jewelry can catch on components or conduct electricity, so it should be removed before working on hardware.
Damaged tools can slip or fail and cause injuries, so they should be replaced.
Working long periods without breaks causes fatigue and strain, which increases the chance of injury.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.4 question 5

stem: Which safety precaution should be taken when disposing of old computer equipment?
options: Recycle the equipment according to local regulations
Disassemble the equipment without protective gear
Throw the equipment in regular household waste
Store the equipment in a humid environment
explanation: Disposing of old computer equipment should be done responsibly by recycling it according to local regulations. This helps prevent environmental contamination and ensures the proper handling of potentially hazardous materials.
whyWrong: Taking equipment apart without protective gear can expose a person to sharp edges and hazardous materials.
Electronic equipment contains hazardous materials and must not go into household waste.
A humid environment causes corrosion and does nothing to dispose of the equipment properly.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.4 question 7

stem: Which of the following safety precautions should be followed when working with high-voltage equipment?
options: Wear insulated gloves and safety glasses
Use a metal ladder when working at heights
explanation: When working with high-voltage equipment, it is essential to wear insulated gloves and safety glasses. These safety measures protect against electric shocks and potential eye injuries. A+ technicians should leave work inside high-voltage devices, such as power supplies, to qualified electricians.
whyWrong: Working alone with high voltage is unsafe because no one is there to help if an accident happens.
A metal ladder conducts electricity, so a nonconductive ladder should be used near electrical equipment.
Damaged cords can expose live wires and cause shocks or fires, so they must be replaced.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.4 question 8

stem: What safety measures should be taken when installing or replacing computer hardware components?
options: Use proper lifting techniques for heavy components
Use excessive force when inserting connectors
Install components in an unventilated area
explanation: When installing or replacing computer hardware components, it is important to use proper lifting techniques for heavy components. This helps prevent strains, back injuries, and damage to the hardware.
whyWrong: Excessive force can bend pins or break connectors, so connectors should be aligned and pressed gently.
An unventilated area can let heat or fumes build up and is not a safe place to install components.
Not grounding yourself lets static discharge damage components, so use an ESD strap or mat.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.4 question 10

stem: Marco, a technician at a small insurance agency, must replace a failed hard drive in a desktop. He has an antistatic strap in his bag and the PC is still running. What should he do FIRST?
options: Shut down the PC and disconnect it from power
Clip the antistatic strap to the case
Open the case and remove the old drive
Place the new drive on top of its antistatic bag
explanation: Personal safety comes first: turn the computer off and disconnect it from AC power before any work inside it. After that, the technician can ground himself and handle the parts.
whyWrong: The strap protects the parts from static, but it does not protect the technician from live power, so power comes first.
Opening the case of a running computer exposes the technician to electrical shock.
Unpacking the new drive can wait until the power is off and the technician is grounded.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

stem: A help desk technician at a shipping company is asked to move a rack-mount UPS that weighs about half his body weight to a room down the hall. Which action is BEST?
options: Ask a coworker to help and move the unit on a cart
Lift the unit alone by bending at the waist
Drag the unit across the floor by its cables
Lift it alone while keeping the back straight
explanation: As a rule, an item heavier than about a quarter of your body weight needs a second person. A cart reduces the strain and the number of trips.
whyWrong: Bending at the waist puts the strain on the weak lower back muscles and invites injury.
Pulling equipment by its cables can damage them and the unit, and it is still a heavy load.
Good lifting form helps, but a load this heavy should not be lifted by one person.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

stem: At a dental clinic, a technician notices smoke and a small flame coming from a power strip behind the front desk. Someone has already called emergency services. Which extinguisher is the BEST choice for this fire?
options: A Class D metal powder extinguisher
explanation: Electrical fires are Class C fires, so the extinguisher must be rated for Class C, such as a CO2 BC or a multipurpose ABC unit. If the fire grows too big, everyone should leave the building.
whyWrong: Water conducts electricity, so a Class A water extinguisher is dangerous on an electrical fire.
Class D extinguishers are made for burning metals such as sodium, not for electrical fires.
Class B units are rated for flammable liquids; an electrical fire needs a Class C rating.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

stem: Which of the following is an example of an environmental control?
explanation: An HVAC system is an example of an environmental control. An HVAC system controls the temperature, humidity, and ventilation of a room.
whyWrong: Temperature and humidity are conditions that a control manages, not controls themselves.
A surge protector protects against power spikes; it does not control the environment.
A fire extinguisher is safety equipment, not a control of the room's environment.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 28: Operational Procedures, Chapter Review question 8

stem: A surge suppressor safeguards connected equipment by directing surges to the__________.
explanation: Surge suppressors (otherwise known as surge protectors) safeguard the equipment that is connected to them by directing surges to the path of least resistance. It usually means redirecting the current to ground. So, the metal-oxide varistor (MOV) within the surge suppressor will normally redirect to the ground wire of the AC circuit because there is no resistance on that wire.
whyWrong: Conductance is the inverse of resistance; surges are not directed by shortest conductance.
Inductance deals with changes in current, not with where a surge is directed.
Sending a surge to the highest voltage, the hot wire, would make the problem worse.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 20

stem: Which of the following tools are commonly used to remove dust from the inside of a computer? (Select the two best answers.)
explanation: Compressed air and a vacuum are tools commonly used to remove dust and debris from inside a computer. Of course, when you use compressed air, consider doing this outside because the dust and dirt will fly all over the place. Use a vacuum to clean up after you are done. If you do use a vacuum inside a computer, make sure it is an antistatic, computer-ready vacuum, and, importantly, don’t touch any of the components inside the system!
whyWrong: Cotton and alcohol clean rollers, cartridges, or displays, not dust inside a computer.
A feather duster can build up static and cause ESD.
Antibacterial surface cleaner is only for the outside of a computer case.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 37

stem: A coworker has asked for a solution that will prevent file corruption by ensuring a graceful shutdown in the event of a power outage. The user would like at least one hour of uptime if the power goes out. Which of the following should you recommend?
explanation: You should recommend an uninterruptible power supply (UPS). This meets both requirements: It enables the system to gracefully shut down in the event of a power outage, which protects files from corruption, and it can provide an hour of uptime (though that will require a fairly powerful UPS of at least 1500 VA).
whyWrong: A surge protector guards against spikes but gives no power during an outage.
A power strip only adds outlets and gives no power during an outage.
A PDU distributes and monitors power but has no battery for an outage.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 63

stem: A technician is dealing with frequent micro power outages in their area of operation. These outages are typically brief, with the longest occurrence lasting up to five minutes. Which of the following options should the technician employ to effectively address this issue and minimize its impact?
explanation: To mitigate the issue of frequent micro power outages, the technician should utilize an uninterruptible power supply (UPS). Unlike surge suppressors that protect against voltage spikes, a UPS provides temporary power during short outages, ensuring the continuous operation of critical electronic devices. A UPS consists of a battery that automatically engages when a power outage occurs, supplying power until normal power is restored or allowing a controlled shutdown. This safeguards the connected equipment against potential data loss, hardware damage, and disruptions in productivity.
whyWrong: A surge suppressor protects against spikes but gives no power during an outage.
Battery backup is a general term; the book's answer is the UPS, which switches over at once and allows a controlled shutdown.
A CMOS battery keeps BIOS settings; it does not power the computer.
A generator is for long outages and is not needed for outages of a few minutes.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 58
note: The book's own explanation says battery backup is another term for a UPS; the UPS is the term the objectives use and the device that takes over at once during an outage, so the book's answer stands.

stem: What document can aid you if a chemical spill occurs?
explanation: A material safety data sheet (MSDS) defines exactly what a particular chemical substance is, what its potential hazards are, and how to deal with those hazards. HEPA stands for high-efficiency particulate air, as in a HEPA filter. OSHA stands for Occupational Safety and Health Administration. EPA stands for Environmental Protection Agency.
whyWrong: HEPA stands for high-efficiency particulate air, a type of filter, not a document about chemicals.
OSHA is the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, an agency, not a chemical data document.
EPA is the Environmental Protection Agency, an agency, not a sheet that describes a chemical.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 60: Environmental Controls, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: A coworker complains that after the cleaning crew has come through, the keyboard irritates his hands and leaves some green residue. What should you do?
options: Contact the manufacturer of the keyboard.
explanation: Contact the facilities department to see if it has the MSDS for the cleaner. You and/or the facilities department should then treat the irritation according to the MSDS. If this does not work and the problem gets worse, take the coworker to the emergency room. Remove the keyboard from the work environment.
whyWrong: A skin irritation from a cleaner is not a fire, so the fire department is not the right contact.
The residue comes from the cleaning product, so the keyboard manufacturer cannot supply its safety data.
Complaining to OSHA does not treat the irritation; the MSDS for the cleaner explains what to do.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 60: Environmental Controls, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: You are concerned with power outages that occur infrequently and for short periods of time. You don’t want your users’ computers to suffer from potentially harmful restarts. What device should you install for the users’ computers?
explanation: Use an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) to protect a computer from ungraceful shutdowns and restarts that can occur as a result of under-voltage events (brownouts), power failures (blackouts), and other AC failures—which the UPS will monitor for. A surge protector (suppressor) is a power strip that also incorporates a metal-oxide varistor (MOV) to protect against surges and spikes. A line conditioner can level out dirty power but won’t protect against a power outage. An MSDS defines what a particular chemical substance is and how to deal with related hazards.
whyWrong: A surge protector stops surges and spikes but keeps no power running during an outage.
A line conditioner smooths dirty power but does not supply power during an outage.
An MSDS is a document about chemical hazards, not a device that protects against outages.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 60: Environmental Controls, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: What is the term for a total loss of power that lasts for a prolonged period?
explanation: A power failure (blackout) is a total loss of power for a prolonged period. The best protection against power failures is either a UPS (battery backup) or a generator. A surge in electrical power means that there is an unexpected increase in the amount of voltage provided. An under-voltage event (brownout) is a drop in voltage (but not to zero) that can cause computers to shut off.
whyWrong: A surge is an unexpected increase in voltage, not a loss of power.
A spike is a short transient increase in voltage, not a prolonged loss of power.
A brownout is a drop in voltage that does not fall to zero, so it is not a total loss of power.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 60: Environmental Controls, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: You want a cost-effective solution to the common surges that can affect your computer. Which device offers the BEST solution?
explanation: A surge suppressor (or surge protector) is the right solution at the right price. A UPS is a possible solution but costs more than a surge protector and is not necessary in this scenario. A power strip doesn’t necessarily have surge protection functionality; it is simply a strip of outlets for additional connectivity. Rack grounding is done to protect networking equipment and servers that are installed into racks in a data center or server room.
whyWrong: A UPS also handles surges but costs more than needed when only surges are the problem.
A plain power strip only adds outlets and does not necessarily protect against surges.
Rack grounding protects equipment installed in data center racks; it does not stop surges at a computer.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 60: Environmental Controls, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: One of your coworkers just spilled a chemical solvent in a warehouse, and you have been asked to help clean it up. Which of the following must contain information about a chemical solvent's emergency cleanup procedures?
explanation: The material safety data sheet (MSDS) will have the necessary information about the cleanup procedures. The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) is an organization that oversees safety in the workplace. The product label may or may not have this information. A cathode-ray tube (CRT) is a type of monitor that uses a glass tube.
whyWrong: OSHA is an agency that oversees workplace safety, not a document about a specific chemical.
A product label may or may not include the cleanup procedures, so it is not a sure source.
A CRT is a type of monitor that uses a glass tube, not a safety document.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns, Review Questions question 3

stem: You are purchasing an inkjet printer cartridge for home use that you know has an MSDS. How do you obtain the MSDS for this product?
options: The store is required to give you one at the time of purchase.
It's contained in the packaging of the printer cartridge.
You are not legally allowed to have an MSDS for this product.
You should visit the printer cartridge manufacturer's website.
explanation: You can download the MSDS by visiting the printer cartridge manufacturer's website. The store is not required to furnish an MSDS at the time of purchase. The manufacturer is not required to furnish an MSDS with the packaging of the product. You are legally allowed to have an MSDS for products, as per OSHA. You should have them on hand in case of an emergency.
whyWrong: The store is not required to give you an MSDS when you buy the product.
The manufacturer does not have to put the MSDS in the product packaging.
OSHA rules allow you to have an MSDS for a product, so it is not forbidden.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns, Review Questions question 4

stem: You just removed four AA alkaline batteries from a remote-control device. What is the recommended way to dispose of these batteries?
options: Take them to a recycling center.
explanation: Alkaline batteries should be taken to a recycling center. Throwing batteries in the trash is not environmentally responsible. Incinerating batteries is not advisable, since they can explode and will create pollution. Flushing batteries down the toilet is not an acceptable disposal method. Recycling keeps the metals and chemicals in batteries out of landfills.
whyWrong: Throwing batteries in the trash is not environmentally responsible and may be against local rules.
Batteries can explode when burned, and burning them creates pollution.
Flushing batteries down the toilet is never an acceptable way to dispose of them.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns, Review Questions question 11

stem: Which of the following types of batteries are not considered environmental hazards?
explanation: Nickel-metal hydride (NiMH) batteries are not considered environmental hazards. Alkaline batteries used to contain mercury, which is an environmental hazard, so they are assumed to be environmental hazards. Nickel-cadmium (NiCd) batteries and button cell batteries are considered environmental hazards.
whyWrong: Alkaline batteries once contained mercury, so they are still treated as an environmental hazard.
NiCd batteries contain cadmium, a toxic metal, so they are an environmental hazard.
Button cell batteries can contain mercury or other heavy metals, so they are an environmental hazard.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns, Review Questions question 20
note: The chapter says NiMH and Li-ion batteries are not classed as hazardous waste; recycling them is still recommended.

stem: Why would a network administrator ensure they use an Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) when deploying a new virtual host server? (Choose two.)
options: It provides power for the virtual host in the event of total power loss
It provides power for the virtual host for 5 minutes so that the host can be shut down gracefully
It provides temporary power for the virtual host should there be a power loss for a few seconds
It provides power for booting the virtual host
explanation: An Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) is similar to a battery in that it holds a charge and, in the event of a very short power outage, can supply power to the company’s servers. If power loss exceeds a few seconds, a UPS can be used to shut down the virtual host gracefully. The UPS cannot keep the host running if there is a total power loss; that would require a generator.
whyWrong: A UPS battery lasts only minutes, so a long total power loss needs a generator.
A UPS is backup power during an outage; it is not needed to boot the server.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 4: Virtualization and Cloud Computing, Objective 4.2 question 16
note: 220-1101 4.2 (virtualization); mapped to 220-1202 4.5 (uninterruptible power supply).

stem: A user reports to the help desk that they are having problems with their keyboard. The keyboard appears to be undamaged but when the computer technician tried the keyboard, some letters were not working. What should the computer technician do FIRST?
options: Wipe the keyboard with a wet cloth
Clean the keyboard with compressed air
explanation: The keyboard has dust or debris stuck under some of the keyboard keys. You should use compressed air to clean between the keys. You should never vacuum a keyboard as it could suck up any loose keys. If you use a wet cloth, you may damage the electronics underneath the keyboard.
whyWrong: A vacuum can suck up loose keys, so compressed air is the safer first choice.
A wet cloth can let moisture reach the electronics under the keys.
Sticky Keys is an accessibility feature and does not stop letters from typing.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.2 question 15
note: 220-1101 5.2; mapped to 220-1202 4.5 (dust cleanup, compressed air/vacuums).

stem: When working on computer equipment, which of the following safety precautions should be taken?
options: Use compressed air to clean debris from fans and heatsinks
Use a magnetized screwdriver to secure components
Store liquids near the computer to easily access them
Place the computer on an unstable surface
explanation: Using compressed air to clean debris from fans and heatsinks helps maintain proper airflow and prevents overheating. It’s important to clean the components safely and without causing damage.
whyWrong: A magnetized screwdriver can drop screws into the case and can disturb magnetic media, so it is not recommended.
Liquids near a computer can spill and cause short circuits or damage.
An unstable surface can let the computer fall and injure people or damage components.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.4 question 2
note: 220-1102 4.4; mapped to 220-1202 4.5 (compressed air/vacuums for dust cleanup)

stem: Which safety measure should be taken when cleaning the inside of a computer?
options: Spray cleaning solution directly onto components
Clean the computer while it is still powered on
Use a dry cloth to wipe the motherboard
explanation: Using an antistatic vacuum cleaner is a safe way to remove dust and debris from the inside of a computer. It helps prevent the buildup of static electricity and reduces the risk of damaging sensitive components.
whyWrong: Spraying liquid directly onto components can cause short circuits; apply cleaner to a cloth first.
Cleaning a powered-on computer risks electric shock and damage, so it must be turned off and unplugged.
Wiping a motherboard with a dry cloth can build static and snag small components.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.4 question 6
note: 220-1102 4.4; mapped to 220-1202 4.5 (compressed air/vacuums for dust cleanup)

stem: What should be done if a chemical spill occurs in the vicinity of computer equipment?
options: Use a vacuum cleaner to remove the spill
Follow proper procedures for chemical cleanup
Ignore the spill and continue working
explanation: In the event of a chemical spill near computer equipment, it is important to follow proper procedures for chemical cleanup. This may involve using appropriate safety equipment, containment measures, and contacting the appropriate authorities if necessary.
whyWrong: Shutting down the equipment may be needed, but the spill itself still needs the proper cleanup procedure.
A vacuum cleaner can spread a chemical spill or react with it and is not a cleanup procedure.
Ignoring a chemical spill puts people and equipment at risk.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.4 question 9
note: 220-1102 4.4; mapped to 220-1202 4.5 (MSDS documentation for handling and disposal)

stem: Which of the following describes the purpose of material safety data sheets (MSDSs) in relation to handling and disposal of hazardous materials?
options: To provide guidelines for safe transportation of hazardous materials
To document the potential hazards and precautions for using a specific material
To outline the proper procedures for recycling electronic waste
To certify the quality and durability of protective equipment
explanation: Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDSs) are important documents that provide detailed information about potential hazards associated with specific materials. They outline the necessary precautions and safety measures to be followed when handling, using, or disposing of hazardous substances. The purpose of MSDSs is to ensure that individuals have access to accurate and relevant information to minimize the risks associated with hazardous materials.
whyWrong: Transportation rules for hazardous materials are set by shipping regulations, not by the main purpose of an MSDS.
E-waste recycling procedures come from local regulations and recycling programs rather than the MSDS purpose described.
An MSDS describes a material's hazards; it does not certify the quality of protective equipment.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.5 question 1

stem: What is the primary purpose of reviewing material safety data sheets (MSDSs) before handling or disposing of hazardous materials?
options: To assess the financial cost associated with the materials
To determine the expiration date of the materials
To understand the potential health and safety risks
To identify potential sources of the materials
explanation: The primary purpose of reviewing material safety data sheets (MSDSs) before handling or disposing of hazardous materials is to understand the potential health and safety risks associated with the materials. MSDSs provide crucial information about the hazards, precautions, and safe handling procedures for the substances involved. By reviewing the MSDSs, individuals can make informed decisions and take necessary precautions to minimize the risks to their health and safety.
whyWrong: An MSDS describes hazards and precautions, not the financial cost of a material.
Expiration dates are printed on the product or packaging, and they are not the purpose of an MSDS.
Where a material comes from is not the reason to review its safety data sheet.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.5 question 2

stem: Proper battery disposal is essential to protect the environment and prevent hazardous materials from contaminating landfills. Which of the following statements accurately describes the correct way to dispose of used batteries?
options: Place used batteries in the regular trash bin
Take the batteries to a nearby electronics store for disposal
Recycle used batteries at designated recycling centers or facilities
Bury the batteries in the backyard to decompose naturally
explanation: Recycling used batteries at designated centers or facilities ensures proper handling and environmentally friendly disposal. Batteries contain chemicals and heavy metals that can leak from landfills, so they must be recycled.
whyWrong: Batteries in regular trash can leak harmful chemicals in landfills.
Some stores accept batteries, but it is not a standard practice everywhere, so designated recycling centers are the correct choice.
Buried batteries do not decompose safely; they leak toxic chemicals into the soil.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.5 question 3

stem: When disposing of toner cartridges from printers and copiers, what is the recommended method to ensure proper disposal?
options: Place the toner cartridges in any nearby recycling bin for regular waste collection
Throw the toner cartridges in the trash as they are not considered hazardous waste
Return the used toner cartridges to the manufacturer or a designated recycling program
Burn the toner cartridges to reduce waste volume before disposing of them
explanation: Returning used toner cartridges to the manufacturer or participating in a designated recycling program ensures they are properly recycled and disposed of in an environmentally responsible manner. Many manufacturers include a prepaid return label or run a take-back program so cartridges can be refilled or recycled.
whyWrong: Ordinary recycling bins are not designed for toner cartridges, and the toner can contaminate other recycling.
Toner cartridges contain materials that should not go to a landfill, so they must not go in the trash.
Burning toner cartridges releases harmful fumes, and toner dust can ignite.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.5 question 4

stem: When disposing of other electronic devices and assets, which of the following methods should you avoid to ensure data security and prevent environmental damage? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Selling the devices to an unknown individual or entity
Donating the devices to a local charity or non-profit organization
Erasing all the data from the devices before recycling or disposal
Disassembling the devices and disposing of their parts separately
explanation: Selling devices to unknown parties may lead to data breaches or unauthorized access to sensitive information. Disassembling devices and disposing of their parts separately without proper knowledge can lead to environmental damage, and some components need specialized recycling facilities. Donating devices is an accepted reuse method once the data has been securely wiped, and erasing the data is a required step before any reuse, recycling, or disposal. Proper disposal often involves data wiping, recycling, or returning the devices to the manufacturer or designated recycling programs.
whyWrong: Donating devices to a charity is an accepted reuse method when the data has been securely wiped first.
Erasing all data before recycling or disposal protects privacy, so it is a step to take, not one to avoid.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.5 question 5
note: Book answer A, B, and D corrected: donating wiped devices to charity is an accepted reuse method (Exam Cram 2e Chapter 60, Docter Chapter 5), so B is not a method to avoid.

stem: What environmental factors should be considered to maintain optimal equipment performance and longevity?
options: Noise level, cable management, and power supply
Lighting conditions, firewall settings, and antivirus software
Backup systems, network security, and data encryption
explanation: Temperature, humidity, and proper ventilation are important factors to consider for maintaining optimal equipment performance and longevity. Extreme temperatures can cause damage to sensitive components, while high humidity levels can lead to condensation and moisture-related issues. Proper ventilation ensures adequate airflow and helps prevent overheating.
whyWrong: Noise level and cable management do not affect component life the way heat and humidity do.
Firewall settings and antivirus software are security controls, not environmental factors.
Backups, network security, and encryption protect data but are not environmental conditions.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.5 question 6

stem: What device is designed to protect electronic equipment from power surges, under-voltage events, and power failures?
explanation: A UPS is specifically designed to provide backup power during power surges, under-voltage events, and power failures. It offers a continuous supply of power to connected devices, protecting them from potential damage or data loss.
whyWrong: Power over Ethernet delivers power and data over a network cable; it gives no backup power.
Network-attached storage is a file storage device and does not protect against power problems.
A wireless access point connects wireless clients to a network and offers no power protection.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.5 question 7

stem: Which device is used to suppress power surges and voltage spikes?
explanation: A surge protector, commonly referred to as a surge suppressor, is a specialized device created with the purpose of safeguarding electronic devices against sudden increases in voltage and power surges. Its primary function is to absorb and redirect excess electrical energy, shielding the connected devices from potential damage caused by these voltage spikes. By offering this protective barrier, surge protectors play a vital role in maintaining the longevity and reliability of electronic equipment.
whyWrong: Some UPS models include surge protection, but their main job is to provide battery power during outages.
A power inverter converts DC to AC power and is not designed to suppress surges.
A basic power strip only adds outlets, and many models give no protection from surges.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.5 question 8

stem: What is the purpose of using a battery backup system?
options: To provide backup power during outages
explanation: A battery backup system, also known as an Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS), is used to provide backup power to connected devices during power outages. It ensures that critical equipment remains operational and prevents data loss or damage caused by sudden power loss.
whyWrong: A battery backup supplies power and has no effect on network bandwidth.
Protection from electromagnetic interference comes from shielding and placement, not from a battery backup.
Surge suppression is the job of a surge protector, while a battery backup mainly keeps power on during outages.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.5 question 9

stem: What is a recommended practice for location/equipment placement to ensure optimal computer performance?
options: Placing the computer on an uneven surface
Locating the computer near direct sunlight
Positioning the computer away from electrical interference
Stacking multiple computers on top of each other
explanation: Positioning the computer away from electrical interference helps reduce potential disruptions and ensures optimal performance. Equipment should also sit on a stable, level surface with room for airflow and away from heat sources.
whyWrong: An uneven surface makes the computer unstable and can block airflow.
Direct sunlight heats the computer and can cause it to overheat.
Stacking computers blocks their vents and traps heat.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.5 question 10

stem: A technician must choose the BEST method suitable for dust cleanup in a computer system. Which of these is the recommended solution?
options: Blowing compressed air directly into the components
Using a dry cloth to wipe the components
Applying water or liquid cleaning agents on the components
Utilizing a vacuum designed for electronics
explanation: Utilizing a vacuum designed for electronics is a suitable method for dust cleanup, as it minimizes the risk of static discharge and safely removes debris. A vacuum made for electronics removes the dust from the system instead of moving it around.
whyWrong: Blowing compressed air directly into components can push dust deeper into the system.
A dry cloth can build static and cannot reach dust inside small spaces.
Water and liquid cleaners can cause short circuits and corrosion on electronic components.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.5 question 11

stem: Your company has multiple users who work with the same commercial software. What is the BEST type of license to purchase so that your company is in compliance with the EULA?
explanation: You would want to get an enterprise license (sometimes referred to as a “corporate use” license). This allows multiple users to install the software on their systems, and each can accept the end-user licensing agreement (EULA) individually.
whyWrong: Seat licensing is used for other license types, not the usual term for many users of one product.
Commercial license is a broad term, not the standard license for many company users.
An open-source license is free to use and modify, so there is nothing commercial to buy.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 5

stem: A manager suspects that a user has obtained movies and other copyright-protected materials through the use of a BitTorrent client. The incident response tech confirms the suspicion; the user is in violation of company policy. What should the incident response technician do NEXT?
options: Secure the workstation in a limited-access storage facility.
Reprimand the user and apply a content filter to the user’s profile.
Document the incident and purge all policy-violating materials.
explanation: The incident response technician should secure the workstation in a limited-access storage facility until the matter is sorted out. A company can be liable for what its employees download, so the workstation should be securely stored and not disturbed until the matter has been investigated thoroughly. The incident response technician should also contact the network administrator (or network security administrator) and inform them that the user was able to download a BitTorrent client and figure out a way to block the usage of those.
whyWrong: Deleting the materials destroys the evidence needed for the investigation.
Reprimanding the user is the manager's job, and content filters are usually set for the whole network.
The incident should be documented, but purging the materials destroys evidence.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 13

stem: Which of the following is the BEST example of the use of chain of custody?
options: The technician notes the date, time, and who was given the computer.
The technician remembers when and who they gave the computer to.
The technician uses a third party to hand over the computer to the proper authorities.
The technician calls the supervisor after the computer has been transferred.
explanation: Chain of custody is the chronological documentation (written) of evidence pertaining to a computer or other technical device that has prohibited content or has been confiscated. The technician should write (or type) the date, time, and who took custody of the computer next. It’s important for the technician to adhere to the chain-of-custody rules when storing the computer or data. It’s also important to verify that the chain of custody remains intact, so as to ensure evidence is admissible in legal proceedings.
whyWrong: Memory is not written documentation and will not stand up as evidence.
Handing the computer through a third party breaks the chain of custody.
Calling the supervisor is part of first response, not the chain of custody.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 32

stem: In order to preserve evidence for potential litigation, what is the MOST LIKELY action an incident handler will take?
options: Create duplicates of any affected hard drives
Reach out to the cyber insurance company
explanation: This process, known as hard drive cloning, involves making an exact copy of the affected drives. By doing so, the original evidence remains intact and can be securely stored, ensuring its admissibility and maintaining the chain of custody. The 220-1202 objectives list this as a copy of the drive for data integrity and preservation.
whyWrong: Encrypting files protects data but does not preserve evidence.
Contacting the insurer may be needed but does not preserve evidence.
Law enforcement may be informed, but making copies of the drives is what preserves evidence.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 12

stem: A recent security audit within a company has identified the widespread use of several unauthorized software applications on employee’s work desktops, employees are engaged in social media activities using these installed applications. These activities are against the company’s policies. In light of this violation, which of the following should be modified to reflect this new requirement?
explanation: The acceptable use policy (AUP) should be updated to prohibit unauthorized applications and social media use on work desktops. The AUP outlines the rules and guidelines for acceptable behavior and usage of company resources. By explicitly including this restriction in the AUP, the company can address the violation and prevent future instances.
whyWrong: EMM manages mobile devices, not the rules for using company desktops.
An SLA defines the service between a provider and a customer.
DLP prevents the loss of sensitive data, not the use of social media apps.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 35
note: The book's explanation refers to cryptocurrency mining, which does not match the stem; it was reworded for the stem.

stem: A home user downloaded free software from an online gaming site. While installing the downloaded software, the user was prompted to read through a long document with legal phrases and terminology. In order to complete the download, the user was prompted to agree to the terms of use set out within the document. What is being presented to the user in this scenario?
explanation: In this scenario, the most likely agreement being utilized is an end user license agreement (EULA). EULAs are commonly encountered when installing software and typically require users to scroll through the agreement text and click an “Accept” button to indicate their consent to the terms and conditions set forth by the software vendor.
whyWrong: An SLA defines service levels between a provider and a customer.
An NDA protects confidential information.
An MOU outlines an agreement between organizations.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 48

stem: While working at a local office, a technician discovers that multiple copies of home edition software are installed on computers. Which of the following is the MOST LIKELY violation in this scenario?
explanation: In this scenario, the most likely violation is the end user license agreement (EULA). The EULA typically specifies the terms and conditions for using the software, including limitations on the number of installations or the type of edition that can be used. If the technician discovered multiple copies of the home edition software installed on computers, it suggests a violation of the EULA by exceeding the permitted number of installations or using the software inappropriately.
whyWrong: PII is personal data and has nothing to do with software installs.
DRM protects copyrighted content, not the number of software installs.
Open-source licenses allow free use, while this is proprietary home edition software.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 62

stem: When preserving data from a hard drive for forensic analysis, which two options should be given the MOST consideration?
explanation: Preserving data from a hard drive for forensic analysis requires meticulous attention to detail and adherence to proper procedures. Chain of custody is essential in maintaining the integrity and credibility of digital evidence; it involves documenting the custody, control, and transfer of evidence from the time it is acquired until it is presented in court. Data integrity refers to the assurance that the preserved data remains unaltered and uncorrupted throughout the forensic analysis process. Measures such as using write-blockers, making bit-for-bit copies of the hard drive, and employing hash algorithms can help verify the integrity of the data.
whyWrong: Licensing agreements govern software use, not evidence preservation.
Incident documentation matters, but it does not preserve the drive's data.
An MSDS describes chemical hazards, not evidence handling.
Retention requirements cover data storage rules, not forensic preservation.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 63

stem: A pharmaceutical company needs to ensure all new employees are correctly onboarded, which of the following documents must be signed by the employee before being granted login access to the network?
explanation: Before being granted login access to the network, a new employee must sign the acceptable use policy (AUP). The AUP outlines the rules and guidelines for utilizing the organization’s network and technology resources. By signing the AUP, the employee acknowledges their understanding and agreement to abide by the policies set forth, ensuring responsible and secure use of the network.
whyWrong: An MSDS describes the hazards of chemicals.
A EULA is a software license, not a condition for network access.
UAC is a Windows security feature, not a document to sign.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 74

stem: You find illegal materials on a customer’s computer. Your boss commands you to preserve computer evidence until arriving on the scene. What is your boss asking you to begin?
explanation: Your boss is asking you to begin the process of a chain of custody, which is a chronological paper trail of evidence. It is a specific form of documentation. You were the first responder. These cases will be rare, but you should understand the terminology and what to do if you find illegal materials.
whyWrong: Documentation is a general term; preserving evidence for a case is the specific chain of custody process.
You already acted as the first responder; preserving the evidence is the next process.
GDPR is a European data protection regulation, not a process for preserving evidence.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism, Cram Quiz 1 question 1

stem: Which of the following is not one of the steps of the incident response process?
explanation: Nonrepudiation, although an important part of security, is not part of the incident response process. Nonrepudiation means that you have irrefutable proof that a person did something; it might include logs, audit trails, and so on. Eradication, containment, and recovery are all parts of the incident response process.
whyWrong: Eradication, which removes the cause of an incident, is a step of the incident response process.
Recovery, which returns systems to normal operation, is a step of the incident response process.
Containment, which stops an incident from spreading, is a step of the incident response process.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism, Cram Quiz 1 question 2

stem: Which of these is a group of security controls designed to restrict the usage or proliferation of copyrighted software and products?
explanation: Digital rights management (DRM) is a group of security controls that restrict usage or proliferation of copyrighted software and products. An end-user licensing agreement (EULA) is a contract or an agreement between a proprietary software vendor and an end user. A personal use license is meant for one user. For example, a home user might have a computer with a paid personal use license to use Microsoft Windows 11 Home Edition. A midsized to large organization might have enterprise-level or corporate use licenses (such as for Windows 11 Enterprise Edition) that are usually bought in bulk.
whyWrong: A EULA is an agreement between a software vendor and an end user, not a set of security controls.
A personal use license lets one user run the software; it does not restrict copying by technical means.
A corporate use license is a bulk license for an organization, not a group of security controls.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism, Cram Quiz 1 question 3

stem: You are the security administrator for your organization. You have just identified a malware incident. Of the following, what should be your FIRST response?
explanation: Of the listed answers, most organizations’ incident response procedures specify that containment of the malware incident should be first. Next would be the removal of the malware, then recovery of any damaged systems, and finally monitoring (which should actually be going on at all times). But before all of this is the preparation phase; in the scenario, identification was already performed.
whyWrong: Removal of the malware comes after it has been contained so that it cannot spread.
Recovery of damaged systems comes after the malware has been contained and removed.
Monitoring should go on all the time, but it is not the first response to a found incident.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism, Cram Quiz 1 question 4
note: The incident response steps (containment, eradication, recovery) are Security+ background; mapped to 220-1202 4.6 incident response.

stem: Which type of regulated data is specifically protected under the HIPAA Privacy Rule?
explanation: Protected health information (PHI) is information that is protected under the HIPAA Privacy Rule.
