The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) is a wide-ranging act that governs the protection of all kinds of health information. Personally identifiable information (PII) is information used to uniquely identify, contact, or locate a person.
whyWrong: PII identifies, contacts, or locates a person; the HIPAA Privacy Rule protects health information.
PCI covers credit cards, debit cards, ATMs, and point-of-sale systems, not health information.
GDPR is a European Union regulation on data protection and privacy, not a type of data under HIPAA.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism, Cram Quiz 1 question 5

stem: A company asks you to sign an NDA before showing you company information. Why is the company asking you to sign the document?
options: The company is going to show you illegal information.
The company is going to show you confidential information it wants to keep secret.
The company wants to collect your Social Security number.
The company wants to hire you.
explanation: The purpose of an nondisclosure agreement (NDA) is to protect confidential information. The company is going to show you information, and it doesn’t want you to share this information with others. It isn’t illegal to do this, and the information is not illegal.
whyWrong: Asking you to sign an NDA is legal, and the information it protects is not illegal.
An NDA protects confidential information; it is not used to collect a Social Security number.
An NDA does not mean a job offer; it only keeps the information you see confidential.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism, Cram Quiz 1 question 6

stem: Which of the following would typically be included in an acceptable use policy (AUP) for an organization?
options: Permission to share company data with external parties at will
Guidelines for ethical and responsible use of the organization's IT resources
Prohibition of personal use of the network
Requirement to use the organization’s network for personal financial transactions
explanation: Acceptable use policies (AUPs) are all about what should and what should not be done on and with the company’s electronic resources. Ethics and responsible use are paramount. If you read the other answers, they just don’t make any sense at all. An AUP describes what users may and may not do with the organization's computers, network, and data.
whyWrong: An AUP protects company data, so it does not let users share that data with outsiders at will.
An AUP sets rules for use of company resources; a total ban on personal use is not what it typically states.
No AUP requires users to do personal financial transactions on the company network.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism, Cram Quiz 1 question 7

stem: You are a field technician working at a customer’s site. One of the workers asks you to load a copy of an organization’s purchased software on a personal laptop. What should you do FIRST?
options: Verify that the installation is allowed under the company’s licensing agreement.
Act as though you are distracted and ignore the user.
Leave the premises and inform the police.
Tell the worker that installing unlicensed software is illegal.
Notify the worker’s manager of a security breach.
explanation: You should check whether the company allows installation of paid software on personal computers or laptops. If it is allowed, go ahead and do the installation. If not, you should refuse and notify your manager of the occurrence. Refusal can be tough at times, so be strong and think about the consequences of your actions. They could directly affect you in a negative way.
whyWrong: Pretending to be distracted and ignoring the worker is unprofessional and does not answer the request.
Leaving and calling the police is an overreaction; the request may even be allowed by the license.
You do not yet know whether the installation is unlicensed; check the licensing agreement first.
A request to install software is not a security breach; check the license before involving a manager.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism, Cram Quiz 2 question 4

stem: Your company's AUP states that employees must not use company resources for personal gain. You have a side business and want to use your work computer to manage it. What should you do?
options: Use your work computer to manage your side business.
Use your personal computer to manage your side business.
Ask your manager for permission to use your work computer.
Ignore the AUP and use your work computer anyway.
explanation: Using your personal computer to manage your side business adheres to the AUP and prevents misuse of company resources. Using your work computer violates the AUP. Asking for permission is unnecessary as the AUP clearly prohibits such use. The AUP sets the rules for how employees may use company computers and networks.
whyWrong: Using the work computer for a side business breaks the AUP rule against personal gain.
The AUP already forbids this use, so asking the manager for permission is not needed.
Ignoring the AUP is a policy violation and can bring disciplinary action.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns, Review Questions question 2

stem: Your office just added 20 new workstations, and your manager has put you in charge of configuring them. The users need to have Microsoft Office installed. What should you do to install Microsoft Office properly on these computers?
options: Ensure that the company has the proper licenses to install 20 additional copies.
Agree with the open source license agreement during installation.
Use the personal license key from an existing system to install Office on the new computers.
Follow normal installation procedures; nothing else needs to be done.
explanation: You should ensure that the company has the proper licenses to install 20 additional copies to be compliant with licensing. Microsoft Office is not an open source licensed product. Using the personal license key from an existing system violates the license agreement. Following normal installation procedures will not ensure compliance of licensing.
whyWrong: Microsoft Office is proprietary software, not an open-source product with an open-source license.
Reusing a personal license key from another system breaks the license agreement.
A normal installation alone does not make sure the company has enough valid licenses.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns, Review Questions question 9

stem: When replacing a hard drive, you discover prohibited material on a user's laptop. What should you do FIRST? (Choose two.)
options: Confiscate and preserve the prohibited material.
Confront the user about the material.
Report the prohibited material through the proper channels.
explanation: The first step is to confiscate and preserve the prohibited materials on the drive. The next step is to report the prohibited materials through the proper channels. Destroying the prohibited material will not remedy the situation. Confronting the user about the material is not suggested, as they could become hostile.
whyWrong: Destroying the material removes evidence and does not deal with the situation.
Confronting the user is not advised because the user could become hostile.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns, Review Questions question 12

stem: You need to investigate how to protect credit card data on your network. Which information should you research?
explanation: You should research information on the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) standard. The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is used for protecting EU citizens. Protected health information (PHI) is any data that defines a patient or an ailment of a patient. Personally identifiable information (PII) is any information that can be used to identify a person.
whyWrong: GDPR is the European Union regulation that protects the personal data of EU citizens, not card data.
PHI is health data about a patient or an ailment, not credit card data.
PII is any data that can identify a person; card data has its own PCI DSS standard.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns, Review Questions question 13

stem: End users are abusing the email system by selling personal items. Which policy would detail the proper use of the email system for business purposes?
explanation: The acceptable use policy (AUP) details the acceptable use of the email system for business purposes. Mobile device management (MDM) is software that allows you to manage mobile devices in the workplace. A password policy details the appropriate handling and management of passwords. Incident management is how a network or security incident is handled.
whyWrong: MDM is software that manages mobile devices, not a policy for using email.
A password policy covers how passwords are handled, not what email may be used for.
Incident management covers how incidents are handled, not the proper use of email.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 7

stem: The FBI informs a business that one of their employees might be carrying out some criminal activities. They want to ensure that any messages sent via corporate email are retained and not deleted as these emails might be needed as evidence for the case against the employee. Which of the following solutions will the system administrator implement?
explanation: A legal hold means that a mailbox has no mailbox limit, and any deleted emails are retained in a purges folder. This prevents a user under investigation from deleting emails. Chain of custody refers to the bagging, tagging, and signing over of evidence to anyone handling the data to prove to the judge that it is the original evidence.
whyWrong: A scheduled backup misses messages that are deleted between backups, so it does not preserve all evidence.
A forensic toolkit extracts data from a computer, but it cannot recover mail purged from the server.
Chain of custody records who handles evidence; it does not stop the employee from deleting emails.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.4 question 22
note: 220-1101 1.4 (mobile device application support); mapped to 220-1202 4.6 (incident response, data preservation).

stem: Two companies plan a long-term partnership to build a product together. Each company will share its own trade secrets with the other. Which agreement BEST protects both companies' information?
explanation: A mutual non-disclosure agreement binds both parties to keep each other's confidential information secret. It fits a partnership where both sides share data. A one-way NDA protects only the disclosing party.
whyWrong: A one-way NDA protects only the party that discloses information, not both companies.
An AUP sets rules for using an organization's technology resources, not for sharing trade secrets.
A EULA sets the terms for using a piece of software, not for protecting business secrets.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

stem: A company is implementing regulatory compliance requirements for its documentation and support systems. It wants to ensure that users are informed about the organization’s policies and procedures before accessing the system. Which of the following best practices should it implement?
explanation: Splash screens are an effective way to communicate important information to users before they access a system. They can display regulatory compliance requirements, organization policies, and other essential information. By implementing splash screens, the company can ensure that users are informed and aware of the necessary guidelines and procedures.
whyWrong: Password complexity rules strengthen accounts but do not show users the organization's policies before they sign in.
Network segmentation divides a network for security and performance; it does not inform users about policies.
Incident reports record events after they happen; they do not present policies to users before access.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.1 question 1
note: 220-1102 4.1 (splash screens); mapped to 220-1202 4.6 (regulatory and business compliance requirements)

stem: Which of the following is an example of a best practice for complying with regulatory requirements related to incident reporting?
options: Implementing splash screens on all company devices
Encrypting sensitive customer data during transit
Training employees on data handling and privacy policies
explanation: Training employees on data handling and privacy policies is a best practice for complying with regulatory requirements related to incident reporting. By providing proper training, employees are equipped with the necessary knowledge and skills to handle incidents appropriately, ensuring compliance with regulatory guidelines. This includes understanding incident reporting procedures, incident classification, and the importance of documenting incidents accurately.
whyWrong: Splash screens display policy notices at sign-in but do not teach staff how to report incidents.
Vulnerability assessments find security weaknesses; they do not address how incidents are reported.
Encrypting data in transit protects confidentiality but is not an incident reporting practice.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.1 question 3
note: 220-1102 4.1; mapped to 220-1202 4.6 (regulatory and business compliance requirements)

stem: Which of the following statements BEST describes an acceptable use policy (AUP) in relation to documentation and support systems information management?
options: An AUP outlines the procedures for creating backups of critical data
An AUP establishes guidelines for the appropriate use of computer systems and networks
An AUP specifies the steps to troubleshoot and resolve hardware-related issues
An AUP defines the process for documenting software license agreements
explanation: An acceptable use policy (AUP) is a set of rules and guidelines that define the acceptable and appropriate use of computer systems and networks within an organization. It outlines the expected behavior of users and helps protect against misuse or abuse of resources. AUPs typically cover topics such as authorized access, prohibited activities, confidentiality, and consequences for non-compliance.
whyWrong: Backup procedures are covered by a backup policy, not by an acceptable use policy.
Hardware troubleshooting steps belong in standard operating procedures or knowledge base articles, not an AUP.
Software license agreements are handled by licensing and compliance records, not by an AUP.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.1 question 14
note: 220-1102 4.1 (types of documents); mapped to 220-1202 4.6 (acceptable use policy)

stem: Which concept ensures the integrity and preservation of data during an incident response in relation to prohibited content/activity?
explanation: The chain of custody is the process of documenting the handling and transfer of evidence during an incident response. It ensures the integrity and preservation of data by maintaining a clear record of who had control over the evidence at any given time.
whyWrong: Incident escalation passes an incident to a higher level of support; it does not preserve evidence.
Password recovery restores access to an account and has nothing to do with evidence handling.
Data compression reduces file size and does not protect the integrity of evidence.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.6 question 1

stem: When encountering prohibited content/activity during an incident response, which action should be taken?
options: Inform management or law enforcement, if necessary
Continue the investigation without involving anyone else
explanation: When encountering prohibited content/activity during an incident response, it is important to inform management or law enforcement, if necessary. This ensures that appropriate actions are taken to address the issue and comply with legal requirements.
whyWrong: Investigating alone without reporting can break policy and legal requirements for prohibited content.
Deleting the content destroys evidence that management or law enforcement may need.
Rebooting the system can destroy volatile evidence and does not address the incident.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.6 question 2

stem: What is the purpose of making a copy of a drive during an incident response?
options: To preserve data integrity and evidence
To speed up the incident resolution process
To minimize the impact on system performance
To reduce the risk of future incidents
explanation: Making a copy of a drive during an incident response is done to preserve data integrity and evidence. It ensures that the original data remains intact and can be analyzed without any modifications.
whyWrong: Copying a drive can take time, and its purpose is to preserve evidence rather than speed up resolution.
A drive copy is made to protect evidence, not to reduce the performance impact on the system.
Making a copy of a drive preserves evidence of the current incident and does not prevent future ones.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.6 question 3

stem: Which concept involves documenting the handling and transfer of evidence during an incident response?
explanation: The concept that involves documenting the handling and transfer of evidence during an incident response is the chain of custody. It ensures a clear record of who had control over the evidence at any given time.
whyWrong: Incident containment stops an incident from spreading; it does not record who handled the evidence.
Data classification labels data by sensitivity and is not a record of evidence handling.
System hardening reduces a system's attack surface and does not track evidence.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.6 question 4

stem: What is the purpose of documenting an incident during an incident response?
options: To provide a reference for future incidents
To inform management of ongoing activities
To facilitate collaboration with other teams
To create a detailed record for analysis and accountability
explanation: Documenting an incident during an incident response serves the purpose of creating a detailed record for analysis and accountability. It provides a comprehensive account of the incident, aiding in understanding the root cause and taking appropriate actions.
whyWrong: A record can help with future incidents, but the main purpose is a detailed account for analysis and accountability.
Informing management is one use of the documentation, but it is not its main purpose.
Documentation can help teams work together, but its main purpose is analysis and accountability.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.6 question 5

stem: Which concept defines the terms and conditions under which software can be used by an individual or organization?
explanation: The end-user license agreement (EULA) outlines the permissions, restrictions, and liabilities associated with the use of software by an individual or organization. The user must accept the EULA before installing or using the software.
whyWrong: A privacy policy explains how an organization collects and uses personal data, not how software may be used.
An open-source license covers the use, change, and sharing of source code, not the general terms of all software.
DRM is technology that controls access to and copying of content; it does not state the license terms.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.6 question 6

stem: What distinguishes a personal use license from a corporate use license?
options: Personal use licenses require individual registration, while corporate use licenses allow multiple users
Personal use licenses have shorter validity periods compared to corporate use licenses
Personal use licenses have fewer restrictions on usage compared to corporate use licenses
Personal use licenses are free, while corporate use licenses require a fee
explanation: Personal use licenses typically require individual registration, allowing the software to be used by a single user for personal purposes. On the other hand, corporate use licenses are designed for organizations and allow the software to be used by multiple users within the organization.
whyWrong: License validity periods depend on the product and the agreement, not on whether it is personal or corporate.
Personal-use licenses usually have more restrictions, such as no commercial use, not fewer.
Personal-use licenses are not always free, and some corporate licenses cost nothing.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.6 question 7

stem: Which licensing concept ensures that users comply with the terms of the software license and prevents unauthorized copying or distribution?
explanation: Digital rights management (DRM) is a licensing concept that focuses on copyright protection and access control to digital content. It ensures that users comply with the terms of the software license and prevents unauthorized copying or distribution.
whyWrong: An open-source license allows copying and sharing of code, so it does not prevent distribution.
A valid license gives the right to use the software but does not technically stop unauthorized copying.
A non-expired license is still in force, but it does not enforce the license terms by itself.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.6 question 8

stem: What is the purpose of licensing/digital rights management (DRM)/the end-user license agreement (EULA) in relation to prohibited content/activity?
options: They facilitate the sharing of prohibited content/activity
They prevent the use of prohibited content/activity
They monitor and report the use of prohibited content/activity
They establish penalties for the use of prohibited content/activity
explanation: Licensing, digital rights management (DRM), and the end-user license agreement (EULA) are designed to prevent the use of prohibited content/activity. They outline the permissible uses of software and help restrict or block access to content or activities that are deemed prohibited or illegal.
whyWrong: Licensing, DRM, and EULAs restrict prohibited use; they do not help anyone share it.
These controls set and enforce permitted use rather than monitoring and reporting violations.
Penalties come from laws and contracts, while licensing, DRM, and EULAs mainly prevent prohibited use.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.6 question 9

stem: Which type of license allows users to view, modify, and distribute the source code of software?
explanation: An open source license allows users to view, modify, and distribute the source code of software. It promotes collaboration, transparency, and community-driven development.
whyWrong: A privacy policy explains how personal data is handled and gives no rights to source code.
A EULA for commercial software usually forbids viewing or modifying the source code.
DRM restricts copying and access to content, so it does not allow distribution of source code.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.6 question 10

stem: Which of the following BEST describes regulated data in the context of privacy and policy concepts?
options: Data that is subject to government regulations and restrictions
Data that is freely accessible to the public
Data that is stored without any encryption or security measures
Data that is shared among employees within an organization
explanation: Regulated data refers to information that is subject to government regulations and restrictions. This type of data may include personal government-issued information, credit card transactions, healthcare data, and other sensitive information that requires special protection and compliance with specific policies.
whyWrong: Data that is freely available to the public is the opposite of regulated data.
Unencrypted storage is a security weakness, not a definition of regulated data.
Data shared among employees is not regulated just because it is shared internally.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.6 question 11

stem: Which type of data is considered as personally identifiable information (PII)?
explanation: Personally identifiable information (PII) refers to data that can be used to identify an individual. Examples of PII include names, addresses, social security numbers, email addresses, and other similar personal details. Protecting PII is crucial for maintaining privacy and complying with privacy regulations.
whyWrong: Social media posts may contain personal details, but posts in general are not the standard example of PII.
Publicly available company information is about an organization, not about an individual.
Non-sensitive email messages do not by themselves identify a person.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.6 question 12

stem: Which of the following describes a key concern when handling credit card transactions?
explanation: When handling credit card transactions, one of the key concerns is securing cardholder data. It is crucial to protect credit card information to prevent unauthorized access, fraud, and identity theft. Compliance with industry standards such as the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) is essential for safeguarding cardholder data.
whyWrong: Data availability matters, but the key concern for card payments is protecting the cardholder data.
Accurate financial records are an accounting concern, not the main security concern for card data.
Transaction speed is a performance goal and does not protect cardholder data.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.6 question 13

stem: Which of the following is an example of personal government-issued information?
explanation: A driver’s license number is an example of personal government-issued information. It is a unique identifier issued by the government to individuals for the purpose of driving legally. Protecting personal government-issued information is important to prevent identity theft and misuse.
whyWrong: Social media usernames are chosen by the user and are not issued by a government.
Wi-Fi passwords are network credentials and are not government-issued information.
A home address is PII, but it is not an identifier issued by a government.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.6 question 14

stem: Which of the following BEST describes data retention requirements?
options: The amount of time it takes to process data
The policies and procedures for storing and managing data
The frequency at which data is backed up
The speed of data transmission over a network
explanation: Data retention requirements refer to the policies and procedures for storing and managing data. It includes determining how long data should be retained, what types of data should be stored, and how data should be protected and disposed of when no longer needed. Compliance with data retention requirements is essential for regulatory compliance and effective data management.
whyWrong: Data processing time is a performance measure, not a retention requirement.
Backup frequency is part of a backup plan, while retention defines how long data is kept.
Data transmission speed is a network measure and has nothing to do with retention.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.6 question 15

stem: Which of the following would be most appropriate for the workplace? (Select two.)
explanation: Khaki trousers and a polo shirt trump jeans and a T-shirt every time. Match the attire to the environment: business casual is the usual minimum for a technician at a client site.
whyWrong: A T-shirt, even a clean one, is too casual for most business workplaces.
Jeans, even pressed ones, are usually too casual for a business casual workplace.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 1: Safety and Professionalism, Chapter Review question 1

stem: While manning the help desk, you get a call from a distraught user who says she has a blank screen. What would be a useful follow-up question? (Select two.)
explanation: Go for the simple answer first. When faced with a blank screen, check to see if the computer and the monitor are turned on.
whyWrong: Asking about a reboot comes later; first confirm that the computer and monitor are even powered on.
An open question about what the user did can sound like blame and does not check the simple causes first.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 1: Safety and Professionalism, Chapter Review question 2
note: 220-1102 4.7 (clarify customer statements); mapped to 220-1202 4.7 (ask questions to narrow the scope of the issue).

stem: When is it appropriate to yell at a user?
options: When he screws up the second time.
When he screws up the fifth time.
explanation: Don’t get angry or yell at clients. Do not argue with a customer or become defensive, even when the situation is difficult.
whyWrong: A technician stays calm and professional no matter how many times a user makes a mistake.
Interruptions are handled politely; yelling at a user is never acceptable.
Repeated mistakes call for patience and training, not yelling.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 1: Safety and Professionalism, Chapter Review question 4

stem: When troubleshooting a software problem on Phoebe’s computer and listening to her describe the problem, you get a text from your boss. Which of the following is the most appropriate action for you to take?
options: Excuse yourself, walk out of the cubicle, and text your boss.
Pick up Phoebe’s phone and dial your boss’s number.
Wait until Phoebe finishes her description and then ask to use her phone to call your boss.
Wait until Phoebe finishes her description, run through any simple fixes, and then explain that you need to call your boss on your cell phone.
explanation: Focus on the customer and don’t use her things. Personal calls and texts are distractions that wait until the customer has your full attention for her issue.
whyWrong: Walking out to text your boss interrupts the customer and shows that she is not your priority.
A technician never uses the customer's phone or other personal items for their own calls.
Asking to use the customer's phone is still using her things for your own business.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 1: Safety and Professionalism, Chapter Review question 5

stem: You are at a customer’s workstation to install several software and hardware updates, a process that will take a while and require several reboots of the computer. What should you do about the password to the user’s account?
options: Require the customer to sit with you throughout the process so she can type in her password each time.
Ask the user to write down her password for you to use.
Ask the user to change her password temporarily for you to use.
explanation: In this circumstance, asking for a temporary password is the right answer. Make sure the user changes her password back before you leave the site.
whyWrong: Making the customer sit through hours of updates and reboots wastes her time.
A written password can be lost or seen by others and breaks basic password security.
Calling a supervisor is not needed for a routine situation with a standard solution.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 1: Safety and Professionalism, Chapter Review question 6
note: 220-1102 4.7; mapped to 220-1202 4.7 (handle customers' confidential and private materials).

stem: Which of the following is a good practice after completing a troubleshooting call at someone’s office?
options: Follow up with a call within a couple of days to make sure everything is going well with the fixed computer.
Make copies of any passwords you used at the site for future reference.
Document any particularly important people you met for future reference.
Do nothing. Your work is finished there.
explanation: A simple follow-up builds goodwill and trust. This is a very important step to take after completing a job.
whyWrong: Copying the passwords used at a site is a security risk, not a good practice.
Keeping notes about people you met is not part of finishing a troubleshooting call.
Doing nothing skips the follow-up that confirms the customer is satisfied.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 1: Safety and Professionalism, Chapter Review question 7

stem: You are a technician working at a help desk in tier 1 support, and you receive a call from a user whose computer is suffering from BSODs. Just as you receive the call, you realize that you are scheduled to take your break. What should you do NEXT?
options: Ask another technician to take the call for you.
Ask the user to call back.
Send the user to help desk tier 2.
Troubleshoot the problem for the user.
explanation: The best answer listed is to ask another technician to take the call for you. In a typical help desk environment, breaks are scheduled, and you don’t want to miss your break because you probably won’t be able to take it later!
whyWrong: Asking the user to call back is poor customer service and may lead to a complaint.
Escalating to tier 2 is premature, since you have not yet looked at the problem.
Starting to troubleshoot right before your break means you cannot give the user full attention.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 4

stem: You just got your first IT job working at a help desk. You get a call from a user about an issue you have never seen before, and you are not sure where to begin troubleshooting. What is the FIRST course of action you should take?
options: Tell the customer that this is the first time you have encountered this problem and to please be patient.
Tell the customer that the problem needs to be escalated to a higher-tier technician.
Tell the customer to please hold while a senior technician is consulted regarding the problem.
Ask the customer if they would mind holding for no more than 2 minutes to check resources.
explanation: Most help desks’ standard policy is to have their techs research new problems for a couple minutes before escalating them to higher-level techs. Often this approach proves to be the right course because the technician is often able to find the answer within 2 or 3 minutes. Of course, if you do place the customer on hold, watch the time (I suggest a timer app) and be sure to get back to that person when that time is up.
whyWrong: Saying it is your first time with the problem lowers the customer's confidence in you.
Escalating right away skips a quick check of the resources that often finds the answer.
Consulting a senior technician at once skips your own short research first.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 34

stem: Which of the following statements describe how to demonstrate professionalism when dealing with a customer? (Select the three best answers.)
options: Meet expectations that the customer sets for you.
explanation: Professionalism comes in many forms. When dealing with a customer, you should avoid distractions, avoid being judgmental, and meet expectations that are set. Also, avoid arguing, talking to coworkers, and engaging in personal interruptions. Be positive and listen to the customer.
whyWrong: Chain of custody is about tracking evidence, not about professionalism.
The technician writes the documentation; it is not left to the customer.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 75

stem: Why would a support technician set their mobile to silent before visiting a customer?
options: To avoid disrupting the customer’s environment
To conserve battery life during the visit
To prevent incoming calls from being recorded
To enable location tracking for service records
explanation: Setting a mobile device to silent or vibrate mode is a courteous practice when visiting a customer because it prevents incoming calls or notifications from causing disruptions or distractions during the visit. It shows respect for the customer’s environment and ensures professional interaction.
whyWrong: Saving battery is not the reason; the reason is to avoid distractions.
Silent mode has nothing to do with call recording.
Silent mode has nothing to do with location tracking.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 14

stem: While troubleshooting an issue with a computer that contains sensitive information, a technician determines that the computer needs to be taken off-site for repair. What should the technician do NEXT?
options: Remove the hard disk drive (HDD) and then send the computer for repair
Delete the sensitive information before the computer leaves the building
explanation: In this scenario, it is crucial for the technician to consult the corporate policies regarding the handling of sensitive information and off-site repairs. Corporate policies provide guidelines and procedures to ensure the protection of sensitive data during such situations. By checking the policies, the technician can make informed decisions on how to proceed with the repair process while maintaining the security and integrity of the sensitive information.
whyWrong: Removing the drive first may break the repair and skips the policy check.
Deleting data before checking the policy may break the rules for handling it.
Manager authorization may be needed, but the policies come first.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 11: Mock Exam: Core 2 (220-1102), Mock Exam question 77
note: 220-1102 4.6; mapped to 220-1202 4.7 (handle confidential and private materials). Option C had a typo (buildin), fixed.

stem: How will speaking with a lot of jargon make a technician sound?
explanation: Using too much computer jargon can make an end user think that you do not have the qualifications needed and are masking it with techno-babble. Use plain language that the customer understands instead.
whyWrong: Heavy jargon does not make a technician sound competent; it can hide a lack of skill.
Customers do not hear heavy jargon as smart; they may think you are masking a lack of knowledge.
Jargon does not make a technician sound powerful; it confuses the customer instead.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism, Cram Quiz 2 question 1

stem: A customer experiences a server crash. When you arrive, the manager is upset about this problem. What do you need to remember in this scenario?
options: Stay calm and do the job as efficiently as possible.
Immediately start troubleshooting without acknowledging the manager’s concerns.
Avoid the customer and get the job done quickly.
Refer the customer to your supervisor.
explanation: There isn’t much you can do when a customer is upset except stay calm and fix the problem! Remember, it’s a job; it’s not personal.
whyWrong: Ignoring the manager's concerns is dismissive and makes a difficult situation worse.
Avoiding the customer is unprofessional; you should stay calm and keep them informed.
You can handle an upset customer yourself; referring them to a supervisor is not needed here.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism, Cram Quiz 2 question 2

stem: Which of the following are good ideas when dealing with customers? (Select two.)
options: Explain to them what they did wrong.
explanation: Speak clearly so that customers understand you and avoid distractions so that the customers know they have your complete attention. Both show the customer respect and help you understand the problem.
whyWrong: Ignoring customers is never good practice; they need to know you are listening.
Telling customers what they did wrong is judgmental and puts them on the defensive.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism, Cram Quiz 2 question 3

stem: You have been asked by a customer at a hospital to perform routine maintenance on a laser printer. Before you begin, you notice that PHI has printed out. What should you do FIRST?
options: Ensure the paper tray is full so that everything can print.
Place the printed output in a secure recycle bin and begin maintenance.
Kindly warn the customer that printing PHI at work is a HIPAA violation.
Ask the customer to move the printed output to another area.
explanation: Ask the customer to move the confidential information. Protected health information (PHI) is information that is protected under the HIPAA Privacy Rule. Before ensuring that the paper tray is full, you should first ask the customer to remove the private information. Remember to always behave professionally and protect people’s privacy.
whyWrong: Filling the paper tray does nothing to protect the confidential output already printed.
You should never throw away or recycle customer printouts unless the customer asks you to.
Printing PHI at a hospital is routine and is not a HIPAA violation.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism, Cram Quiz 2 question 5

stem: You promised a customer that you would be out to service their problem before the end of the day but have been tied up at another site. As it now becomes apparent that you will not be able to make it, what should you do? (Choose the BEST answer.)
options: Arrive first thing in the morning.
Wait until after hours and then leave a message that you were there.
Call the customer and inform them of the situation.
Email the customer to let them know that you will be late.
explanation: Calling the customer and informing them of the situation is the best action that can be performed, since you are having direct communications. Arriving first thing in the morning should be done, but communication is the first action. Waiting until after hours and then leaving a message is not an appropriate action. Sending an email letting the customer know that you will be late is lying, since you will not make it to their site.
whyWrong: Arriving in the morning is fine later, but you must tell the customer about the delay first.
Leaving a message after hours is dishonest and does not keep the customer informed.
An email saying you will be late is misleading because you will not arrive today at all.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 11

stem: A user reports that a workstation has two significant problems that do not seem related. How should you approach these problems?
options: Look for what the two problems would have in common.
Assume that a virus is involved.
explanation: If the problems do not appear to be related, then deal with them separately. Looking for commonalities between the problems would just waste valuable time. No assumptions should be made, such as that a virus is causing the problem, unless there is proof. Ordering a new machine is disruptive to the customer, unless the problem dictates that this action be performed.
whyWrong: Looking for a common cause of two unrelated problems wastes valuable time.
You should not assume a virus without proof that one is involved.
Ordering a new machine disrupts the customer and is not needed unless the problem requires it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 12
note: This troubleshooting approach is mainly 220-1201 5.1; mapped to 220-1202 4.7 (dealing with customer issues).

stem: A customer is trying to explain a problem with their system. Unfortunately, the customer has such a thick accent that you are unable to understand their problem. What should you do? (Choose the BEST answer.)
options: Just start working on the system and look for obvious errors.
Ask that another technician be sent in your place.
Apologize and find another user or manager who can help you translate.
explanation: If you do not understand the customer, you should apologize, treat the customer with respect, and seek a manager to help translate. Ignoring the customer and starting to work on the system is not an appropriate response. Calling your supervisor will not solve the problem, since your supervisor will have the same issue. Asking that another technician be sent in your place is being insensitive to the customer and “passing the buck.”
whyWrong: Working on the system without understanding the problem ignores the customer.
Your supervisor would have the same trouble understanding the customer.
Asking for another technician is insensitive to the customer and passes the problem on.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 13

stem: You have been trying to troubleshoot a user's system all day when it suddenly becomes clear that the data is irretrievably lost. When you inform the customer, they become so angry that they shove you against a wall. What should you do?
options: Shove the user back, only a little harder than they shoved you.
Shove the user back, only a little easier than they shoved you.
Try to calm the user down.
Yell for everyone in the area to come quickly.
explanation: You should avoid confrontations with the user by attempting to calm them down. You should never shove the user back. Yelling for everyone in the area to come quickly will escalate the situation, which is the opposite of what you want to do.
whyWrong: Shoving the user back escalates the confrontation and is never acceptable.
Shoving the user back, even gently, escalates the confrontation and is never acceptable.
Yelling for everyone to come quickly escalates the situation instead of calming it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 14

stem: A customer tells you that a technician from your company spent three hours on the phone making personal calls. What should you do with this information?
options: Ask the customer to prove it.
explanation: You should take appropriate action and inform your manager, as well as notify the customer that you've done so. Doing nothing is not an appropriate response to this situation. Talking to the technician personally will create a confrontation and should be avoided. Asking the customer to prove it is an inappropriate action to this problem.
whyWrong: Doing nothing is not an appropriate response to a customer complaint.
Talking to the technician yourself creates a confrontation and should be avoided.
Asking the customer to prove it is dismissive of the customer's complaint.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 15

stem: You arrive at the site of a failed server to find the vice president nervously pacing and worrying about lost data. What should you do?
options: Offer a joke to lighten things up.
Downplay the situation and tell him that customers lose data every day.
Keep your head down and keep looking at manuals to let him know that you are serious.
Inform him that you've dealt with similar situations and will let him know what needs to be done as soon as possible.
explanation: You should assure the vice president that you are optimistic and skilled to deal with these problems. Offering a joke is an inappropriate action. Downplaying the situation does not show respect to the customer's problem. Keeping your head down and ignoring the customer does not display appropriate communications.
whyWrong: A joke is inappropriate when the customer is worried about lost data.
Downplaying the situation shows no respect for the customer's problem.
Ignoring the customer while reading manuals is poor communication.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 16

stem: You are temporarily filling in on phone support when a caller tells you that they are sick and tired of being bounced from one hold queue to another. They want their problem fixed, and they want it fixed now. What should you do?
options: Inform them up front that you are only filling in temporarily and won't be of much help.
Transfer them to another technician who handles phone calls more often.
Try to solve their problem without putting them on hold or transferring them elsewhere.
Suggest that they call back at another time when you are not there.
explanation: You should try to solve the customer's problem without further escalating the frustration by putting them on hold or transferring them. Informing them that you won't be able to help is only going to anger the caller, further validating their frustration. Transferring them to another technician is not the appropriate action, because it will add to their frustration. Suggesting that they call back will create more frustration and is poor customer service.
whyWrong: Saying you will not be much help only angers the caller further.
Another transfer adds to the frustration of a caller who is already tired of being bounced around.
Asking them to call back later creates more frustration and is poor customer service.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 17

stem: At the end of the day, you finish a job only to find that the user you were doing it for had to leave. What should you do? (Choose two.)
options: Clean up and leave no evidence that you were there.
Leave a note for the user detailing what was done and how to contact you.
Notify the user's manager and your own manager that you have finished.
Put the system back to its original state.
explanation: Leaving a note for the user detailing what was done and how to contact you displays appropriate communications. Notifying the user's manager and your own manager that the problem is resolved is also appropriate communications. Cleaning up and leaving no evidence that you were there is an inappropriate action, as it is deceiving to the user. Putting the system back to its original state is an inappropriate action because it does not solve the problem.
whyWrong: Leaving no trace of your visit deceives the user about the work that was done.
Putting the system back to its original state undoes the work and does not solve the problem.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 18

stem: A user on the phone does not seem to be able to explain their problem to you without using profanity. That profanity is making you unable to understand their problem. What should you do? (Choose the BEST answer.)
options: Ask the user to refrain from the offensive language.
Show them that you know just as many expletives as they do.
explanation: While the user's profanity is likely linked to frustration, it hinders the communication and should be eliminated. You should ask the user to refrain from the offensive language. There may be circumstances where it is necessary to overlook the profanity, if your request is likely to make the already upset customer even angrier, as long as you can understand what is being said. Hanging up is not an appropriate action and will further the user's frustration. Firing back with profanity is not an appropriate response, as it will escalate the situation further.
whyWrong: Overlooking the profanity does not help when it keeps you from understanding the problem.
Hanging up is unprofessional and makes the user more frustrated.
Answering with profanity escalates the situation further.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism, Review Questions question 19

stem: A technician will spend a day at a law firm's office giving desk-side support. The firm has no posted dress code. Which attire is BEST?
options: Business casual, such as dress slacks and a collared shirt
Rugged work clothes and safety boots
explanation: Technicians should match the attire that the work environment expects. For day-to-day support in an office, business casual is the usual choice. Dressing down makes the customer judge the technician as less professional.
whyWrong: Jeans and a T-shirt look unprofessional in an office environment and lower the customer's trust.
Rugged work clothes suit a construction site, not desk-side support in a law office.
Athletic wear is far too casual for an office and does not present a professional appearance.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

stem: A technician arrives to fix a printer in a hospital department. The department head introduces herself as Dr. Amara Okafor. How should the technician BEST address her?
options: As Dr. Okafor, unless she asks to be called something else
As Amara, to keep the visit friendly
With a nickname such as Doc
With no name at all, to avoid getting it wrong
explanation: Using appropriate professional titles is part of being culturally sensitive and respectful. In many settings, leaving out a person's title can be taken as an insult. The technician should use the title unless the customer invites a less formal name.
whyWrong: Using a first name without being invited to can seem disrespectful when the person gave a title.
A casual nickname is unprofessional and does not respect the customer's professional title.
Avoiding her name entirely seems cold, and her name and title were already given clearly.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

stem: When service desk personnel are communicating with customers, which communication technique demonstrates professionalism and empathy?
options: Interrupting the customer to provide quick solutions
Using technical jargon to establish expertise
Active listening and paraphrasing the customer’s concerns
Offering discounts or freebies to resolve the issue
explanation: Active listening and paraphrasing the customer’s concerns demonstrate professionalism by showing that you understand their needs and are actively engaged in finding a solution. Restating the concern back to the customer also confirms that the technician understood the issue correctly.
whyWrong: Interrupting the customer is rude and can cause the technician to miss important details.
Technical jargon confuses many customers, so plain language should be used.
Discounts or freebies do not solve the problem and are not a communication technique.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.7 question 1

stem: Which of the following is an example of non-verbal communication that reflects professionalism?
options: Maintaining eye contact and nodding in agreement
Checking personal emails on a mobile device
Speaking softly to avoid disrupting others
Using slang terms and informal language
explanation: Maintaining eye contact and nodding in agreement are non-verbal cues that demonstrate active listening and engagement, which are professional communication behaviors. These cues show the customer that the technician is paying attention without interrupting.
whyWrong: Checking personal email during a conversation is a distraction and is unprofessional.
Speaking softly may be polite, but it is not the non-verbal cue of professionalism the question asks for.
Slang and informal language are verbal, not non-verbal, and they are unprofessional.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.7 question 2

stem: In a business email, which of the following is the most appropriate way to address the recipient?
explanation: Using “Dear [Recipient’s First Name],” is the most appropriate and professional way to address the recipient in a business email. A formal greeting with the person's name sets a respectful, professional tone.
whyWrong: Hey is too informal for a business email.
To whom it may concern is used when the recipient's name is unknown, not for a known business contact.
Hi there is too casual and does not address the recipient by name.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.7 question 3

stem: Which of the following communication methods is most suitable for conveying complex technical information to a non-technical audience?
options: Using technical terms and acronyms extensively
Utilizing visual aids, diagrams, and illustrations
Speaking rapidly to ensure all information is covered
explanation: Utilizing visual aids, diagrams, and illustrations is the most effective way to convey complex technical information to a non-technical audience. Pictures and diagrams let non-technical people follow the idea without knowing the technical terms.
whyWrong: Heavy use of technical terms and acronyms confuses a non-technical audience.
Written documentation alone may not explain complex ideas well to people without a technical background.
Speaking rapidly makes the information harder to follow and understand.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.7 question 4

stem: Which of the following is an example of appropriate use of professional language in customer communication?
options: “Your device is experiencing some technical difficulties”
explanation: Saying that the device is experiencing some technical difficulties is professional language, because it describes the situation without being overly casual or judgmental. The other statements use unprofessional language and may not effectively address the customer's concerns.
whyWrong: Totally messed up is slang and sounds judgmental, which is unprofessional.
Acting weird is vague, informal slang that does not describe the problem professionally.
Saying the PC is broken is blunt and can alarm the customer without explaining the issue.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.7 question 5

stem: When speaking with a customer, which of the following is a professional way to handle a disagreement or conflict?
options: Raising your voice to assert dominance
Blaming the customer for the issue
explanation: Offering alternative solutions and compromises demonstrates professionalism when handling a disagreement or conflict with a customer. Raising your voice, blaming the customer, or ignoring their concerns are unprofessional and can escalate the situation.
whyWrong: Raising your voice turns a disagreement into an argument and is unprofessional.
Blaming the customer makes them defensive and does not solve the problem.
Ignoring the customer's concerns dismisses their issue and makes the conflict worse.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.7 question 6

stem: Which of the following is an example of appropriate professional behavior when interacting with colleagues?
options: Actively listening and respecting others’ opinions
explanation: Actively listening and respecting others’ opinions is an example of appropriate professional behavior when interacting with colleagues. Respectful listening builds trust and helps the team work well together.
whyWrong: Gossiping about team members damages trust and is unprofessional.
Taking credit for other people's work is dishonest and harms the team.
Criticizing colleagues in public embarrasses them; feedback should be given privately.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.7 question 7
note: 220-1102 4.7; the question is about colleagues rather than customers, mapped to 220-1202 4.7 (actively listen)

stem: Which of the following communication methods is BEST suited for delivering sensitive or confidential information?
options: Public announcement during a team meeting
Sending a mass email to all employees
Posting the information on a public bulletin board
explanation: Holding individual face-to-face meetings is the best communication method for delivering sensitive or confidential information. A private meeting keeps the information between the people who need it and allows questions in confidence.
whyWrong: A public announcement exposes confidential information to everyone in the meeting.
A mass email sends sensitive information to people who should not receive it.
A public bulletin board lets anyone read the information, which breaks confidentiality.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.7 question 8
note: 220-1102 4.7; mapped to 220-1202 4.7 (handle confidential and private materials)

stem: Which of the following is an example of maintaining professionalism in a virtual meeting?
options: Eating a meal while on camera
Keeping the microphone on mute when not speaking
Using informal language and abbreviations in chat messages
explanation: Keeping the microphone on mute when not speaking is an example of maintaining professionalism in a virtual meeting. Muting prevents background noise from distracting the other participants.
whyWrong: Eating on camera is distracting to others and unprofessional in a meeting.
Informal language and abbreviations in chat messages look unprofessional and can be misunderstood.
Irrelevant personal stories waste meeting time and distract from the topic.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.7 question 9

stem: When communicating with customers, which of the following is a professional approach to managing their expectations?
options: Setting realistic expectations and providing updates
Ignoring customer requests to avoid conflicts
Redirecting customers to a different support channel
explanation: Setting realistic expectations and providing updates is a professional approach to managing customer expectations. Regular status updates keep the customer informed and avoid surprises about the timeline.
whyWrong: Overpromising sets expectations the technician cannot meet, which leads to disappointment.
Ignoring customer requests is unprofessional and does not avoid conflict.
Redirecting customers without addressing their concerns can seem dismissive.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.7 question 10

stem: Which of the following actions should a technician take to deal appropriately with a customer’s confidential and private materials stored on a desktop computer?
options: Regularly share the customer’s data with colleagues for collaborative purposes
Encrypt the customer’s sensitive files and folders using strong encryption algorithms
Upload the customer’s confidential data to a cloud storage service for backup
Dispose of the customer’s computer without securely wiping the hard drive
explanation: Encrypting the customer’s sensitive files and folders using strong encryption algorithms ensures their data remains confidential and protected. Only authorized people with the decryption key can read the encrypted files.
whyWrong: Sharing a customer's data with colleagues breaks confidentiality.
Uploading confidential data to a cloud service without the customer's permission can expose it.
Disposing of a computer without wiping the drive leaves the customer's data readable by others.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.7 question 11

stem: When dealing with a customer’s confidential materials on a printer, which of the following steps should a technician take to maintain security?
options: Share the printer’s access credentials with other technicians for easier troubleshooting
Disable logging features on the printer to prevent potential privacy breaches
Implement access controls on the printer to restrict unauthorized usage
Print the customer’s confidential documents in a public area for quick access
explanation: Implementing access controls on the printer ensures that only authorized individuals can use and access the customer’s confidential materials, maintaining their security. Access controls such as PINs or badge release keep printed confidential documents from unauthorized users.
whyWrong: Sharing printer credentials widely increases the risk of unauthorized access to confidential documents.
Logs help track who used the printer, so disabling them does not improve privacy or security.
Printing confidential documents in a public area lets anyone pick them up and read them.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.7 question 12

stem: A technician is helping a customer secure their desktop computer. The technician must implement best practices to protect the customer’s confidential materials. Which offers the BEST solution?
options: Create a shared user account with unrestricted access for the customer and their colleagues
Regularly perform data backups without verifying the integrity and confidentiality of the backup media
Implement strong password policies and enable full disk encryption for the customer’s desktop
Store the customer’s confidential files in publicly accessible folders for easier collaboration
explanation: Implementing strong password policies and enabling full disk encryption on the customer's desktop computer provides an additional layer of security, ensuring the confidentiality of their materials. Strong passwords stop unauthorized sign-ins, and full disk encryption keeps the data unreadable if the drive is removed or stolen.
whyWrong: A shared account with unrestricted access lets anyone see the confidential files.
Backups that are not checked for integrity and confidentiality can fail or expose data.
Publicly accessible folders let anyone read the customer's confidential files.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 10: Operational Procedures, Objective 4.7 question 13

stem: A store manager calls the help desk and starts shouting that the point-of-sale system has failed for the third time this month and that IT is useless. Which response is BEST?
options: Stay calm, let him finish, and say you will help fix it
Explain that the last failure was caused by store staff
Tell him to call back when he is calmer
Transfer him at once to a supervisor
explanation: With a difficult customer, do not argue or get defensive. Let the customer vent, stay calm, and focus on fixing the problem.
whyWrong: Blaming the customer is judgmental and will make the situation worse.
Refusing to help dismisses the customer's issue and leaves the problem unsolved.
Passing the call on at once avoids the problem instead of dealing with it professionally.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

stem: A technician arrives at a law firm to replace a keyboard. The attorney's desk is covered with open client case files, and some pages are next to the keyboard. What is the BEST thing for the technician to do?
options: Ask the attorney to move the files before starting
Stack the files neatly on a chair
Read the top page to judge if it is sensitive
Work around the files without saying anything
explanation: Technicians must not look at or touch a customer's confidential materials. Asking the customer to move them keeps them private and respects the customer.
whyWrong: Moving the files yourself means touching confidential material, which a technician should not do.
Reading the page to judge it is exactly the access to private material that must be avoided.
Working next to the files leaves them in view and risks disturbing them.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

stem: Priya has a 9 a.m. appointment to fix a teacher's projector at a school. At 8:50 she realizes she will be about 20 minutes late. What is the BEST action?
options: Call the teacher, apologize, and give a new arrival time
Arrive late and apologize when she gets there
Send a text to her own manager only
Reschedule the visit for the next day without asking
explanation: Being on time matters, and if a technician will be late, they should contact the customer and apologize. Giving a new time lets the customer plan around the delay.
whyWrong: Arriving late without notice leaves the customer waiting and can sour the visit before it begins.
Telling only her manager does not let the customer know about the delay.
Moving the visit without asking ignores the customer's needs and the agreed time.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

stem:
Which of the following features in Windows allows the following command to run?

```
$PSVersionTable
```
explanation: PowerShell is an advanced command line in Windows that goes beyond the Command Prompt. It is designed for administrators so that they can run scripts, batch commands, and snippets, and save the work as .ps1 files (by default). The command $PSVersionTable will tell you the version of PowerShell, the Windows version, and more. The PS in the command stands for “PowerShell”!
whyWrong: Compatibility mode runs older programs in newer Windows; it does not run commands.
OneDrive is Microsoft's cloud storage service, not a command shell.
Windows Defender Firewall blocks unwanted traffic; it does not run commands.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 8

stem:
You are working at a computer and see the following at the beginning of a script:

```
#!/bin/bash
```
What type of system are you working at?
explanation: This is a Linux, UNIX, or macOS system. When it comes to Linux, UNIX, and similar systems, a lot of technicians simply refer to them as *nix, meaning anything ending in nix. Many Linux distributions use the Bash shell by default. This is where scripts are run. This default line tells the system the path and how to interpret the upcoming script.
whyWrong: Windows uses PowerShell, and its .ps1 scripts do not start with a Bash line.
iOS does not run Bash scripts the way Linux and macOS do.
JavaScript is a scripting language, not a type of system.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 53

stem: You need to write a script that checks data one line at a time until the end of the file being searched. Which of the following constructs should you use?
explanation: You want to use a loop construct, such as a for or while loop, that will loop through a command block until the condition changes from true to false (the end of the file). A loop repeats its block of commands until its condition changes, such as reaching the end of the file.
whyWrong: An integer is a whole number, not a construct that repeats a block of code.
A string is a set of characters, not a construct that repeats a block of code.
A variable holds a value that can change, but it does not repeat commands.
An if-then statement chooses a path once; it does not repeat until the end of the file.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 62
note: Loops are not a listed 220-1202 4.8 sub-topic; mapped to 4.8 (use cases for scripting: gathering of information/data).

stem: You are tasked with creating a new script in PowerShell. You need to add notes to the script to explain to the engineering group what each portion of the script is meant to do. Which of the following should you make use of?
explanation: Use comments to describe what the script is doing. In PowerShell, Bash, and many other scripting systems, use the number sign (#) to start a comment. Remember, comments don’t actually do anything other than provide explanation.
whyWrong: End-user documentation is for users, while comments explain the script to engineers.
Variables and if-then statements make the script do things; they do not explain it.
Change management documentation is needed when you change the script, not to explain its code.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 68
note: Comments are not a listed 220-1202 4.8 sub-topic; mapped to 4.8 (other considerations when using scripts).

stem:
Look at the following syntax:

```
net use Z: \\servername\sharename
```
Which of the following file types would you expect this syntax to be located in?
explanation: The syntax shown is one way of mapping a network drive in Windows. net use is the command, the drive letter to be used is Z:, and the path to the share is \\servername\sharename. This type of command would historically be found in a batch file in Windows; it uses the .bat extension. However, PowerShell is the newer, and better, tool to work with; it uses the .ps1 file extension by default.
whyWrong: .vbs is for Visual Basic scripts, which are not needed to map a drive.
.js is for JavaScript, which is mostly used on websites.
.py is for Python scripts, which are not needed to map a network drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 2 (220-1202) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 79

stem: Which statement about scripting languages is true?
options: Scripting languages have good memory management.
explanation: Scripting languages are interpreted languages that run on top of a runtime environment. Programming languages, not scripting languages, require a compiler. Scripting languages are not strongly typed; programming languages are strongly typed. Scripting languages have bad memory management because of loosely typed variables.
whyWrong: Programming languages, not scripting languages, need a compiler.
Scripting languages are loosely typed; programming languages are the strongly typed ones.
Scripting languages have poor memory management because their variables are loosely typed.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence, Review Questions question 1
note: Programming concepts (types, variables, loops) are background for 220-1202 4.8 scripting; mapped to the closest topic.

stem: What level are scripting languages considered?
explanation: Scripting languages are considered high-level languages because they do not directly access hardware and use an intermediary called the interpreter. Mid-level languages are Java and C/C++, not scripting languages. There is no such thing as an intermediate-level language. Low-level languages are machine language and assembly language, which are not scripting languages.
whyWrong: Mid-level languages are Java and C or C++, not scripting languages.
There is no intermediate level of programming language in this classification.
Low-level languages are machine language and assembly language, not scripting languages.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence, Review Questions question 2
note: Programming concepts (types, variables, loops) are background for 220-1202 4.8 scripting; mapped to the closest topic.

stem: Which type of variable will allow decimal math?
explanation: Floating-point variables allow for precision math, also known as decimal math. Boolean variables allow for true or false values. Integer variables allow for whole numbers values. String variables allow for text values.
whyWrong: A Boolean variable holds only true or false values.
An integer variable holds whole numbers only, so it cannot hold decimal values.
A string variable holds text values, not numbers for math.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 2 – Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence, Review Questions question 3
note: Programming concepts (types, variables, loops) are background for 220-1202 4.8 scripting; mapped to the closest topic.

stem: Which environment variable is not inherited?
explanation: A program variable is the least significant and it is not inherited. A system variable is defined for the entire system and is the most significant because it is inherited by all users and programs. A user variable is significant as well, since all applications will inherit the variable. A string variable is not inherited, but it is not an environment variable.
